Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 47, verse 1:

Consider here how beautifully the end of the previous surah connects with the beginning of this one. At the end of al-Ahqaf: ﴿So will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35], and here: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred [others] from the way of Allah — He has nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 1]. It is as if "the defiantly disobedient" (al-fasiqun) are those who disbelieved and barred from the way of Allah.

Kufr (disbelief) has been defined as concealment: concealing the truth, or concealing the traces of the truth. The word kufr, by its very meaning, implies that something is concealed. And what does disbelief conceal? It conceals its opposite, which is faith (iman). So faith existed first, and then disbelief came to cover it.

Thus the word kufr is the first proof of faith, because faith is a matter of innate nature (fitrah), an instinct within the human soul, while it was still in the realm of the primordial souls (alam al-dharr), when Allah took the covenant from them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'raf: 172].

Disbelief may conceal not the thing itself but its effects, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah presents a parable: a city that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah...﴾ [al-Nahl: 112].

So: "denying Allah" is one thing, and "denying the favours of Allah" is another.

Denial of favour (kufr al-ni'mah) takes several forms. Among its forms is heedlessness toward a favour and not seeking its causes, and not drawing out its potential in the cosmos with what it contains of causes: water, air, and earth.

Consider, for example: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance...﴾ [Fussilat: 9–10].

So: your Lord has given you the causes and commanded you to search into them and draw them out, and not to be lazy in extracting what is in nature of good things. After Allah has given you the causes of blessing, do not be negligent regarding them and live as a beggar, a burden upon others.

A person may search for a blessing and draw it out, but then conceal it from those who deserve it and hoard it from them. Concerning these, Allah said: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 34–35].

So: disbelief is either disbelief in Allah by denying His existence, or disbelief in His blessings and bounties.

As for His words ﴿and barred [others] from the way of Allah﴾ [Muhammad: 1]: it means they prevented people from believing in Allah, or they blocked their ears from hearing the warning of the call to Allah, and blocked their eyes from seeing the signs of Allah in the cosmos and taking them as evidence of the Creator, and blocked their hearts from faith in Allah and accepting certainty.

All of these are objects of "barred" (sadd). So these people disbelieved and were not content with their own disbelief; rather, they tried to drag others into their domain.

For this reason the orientalists have stopped at this matter, saying: "You say the verses are clear (muhkam), yet we find in them an appearance of contradiction, such as His saying: ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ [al-Zumar: 7].

And He says elsewhere: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Nahl: 25]." In truth there is no contradiction between the two verses, because the matter is different: when they went astray themselves, they bore their own burdens, and when they led others astray, they bore the burden of their own misguidance and the burden of misguiding others.

The meaning of ﴿He has nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 1] is that He made them void and without benefit, because misguidance means failing to be guided to the path that leads to the goal. These people did deeds that do not return to them with any benefit. And what benefit is there in disbelief and in barring people from faith?

Even those who do good while outside the domain of faith are not accepted from them, and this good does not intercede for them in the Hereafter, because they did not do it from the standpoint of faith. Rather, they did it from the standpoint of fame, reputation, civilization, and serving humanity, and the rest of these slogans.

Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿And We will turn to whatever deeds they did and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23].

And He says: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty man thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. These are the ones who will be told on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20].

On the other hand, He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾.

We have said that opposites reveal one another, and that mentioning opposites is a feature of the Qur'an's style, so that a comparison is made between the two and the picture becomes clear, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss * And indeed, the wicked will be in the Hellfire﴾ [al-Infitar: 13-14].

Here, in contrast to "those who disbelieve," He says ﴿And those who believe...﴾ [Muhammad: 2], and He did not say "believed in whom," because faith (iman) is a natural matter (fitri), and when it is mentioned unqualified, it refers to faith in God, since that is the first faith.

The verb āmana (to believe) takes the preposition bi (ba'), as in "āmana bihi," meaning he believed in its existence. It also takes the preposition li (lam), as in "āmana lahu," meaning he affirmed him as true. It may also take no preposition, as in ﴿and He gave them security from fear﴾ [Quraysh: 4]. All of these forms convey the meanings of security, tranquility and peace.

His saying ﴿and did righteous deeds...﴾ [Muhammad: 2]: the Qur'an constantly pairs faith with righteous deeds, because faith is the work of the heart, while righteous deeds are the work of the body (qalib) and the limbs (jawarih). From the heart and the body, compliance comes about: a heart's faith in the creed, and a body's faith in obeying the command of the One one believes in.

The master of all the limbs in a human being is the heart, because it is the organ that pumps blood, the fluid of life, to all parts of the body. When the heart is filled with faith, it pumps it to all the organs, and they become upright.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The work of the heart is to believe in God and in what God has told of the unseen: to believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in divine decree, its good and its evil. Then comes the work of the limbs. So your eye does not extend toward what is forbidden to you, your tongue does not bear false witness, does not backbite people, does not slander chaste women, and is not used to swear a false oath. Your belly is not filled except with what is lawful, your hand does not steal with it, does not kill a soul which God has forbidden except by right, and your foot does not walk with it toward what is forbidden."

So: every limb has a righteous deed, and it is required that you keep it away from what is unlawful. Among righteous deeds there is one that includes all the limbs, which is kindness to one's parents. Therefore God linked it to His worship, saying: ﴿Worship God and associate nothing with Him, and to parents be good...﴾ [an-Nisa: 36].

In Surah al-Asr there is a statement of the importance of righteous deeds after faith in God, where He says: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds...﴾ [al-Asr: 1-3].

His saying: ﴿And believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad, and it is the truth from their Lord...﴾ [Muhammad: 2]. His saying ﴿and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad...﴾ [Muhammad: 2], after ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ [Muhammad: 2], indicates the obligation to believe in the earlier messengers.

Therefore He said: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein...﴾ [ash-Shura: 13].

That is because the root of religion is one, which is the worship of God alone. So the matter of faith is one for all the messengers of God. From faith in God branches faith in the books, in the messengers, in the Hereafter and in the reckoning, because you have believed in God.

But does God address you alone and say to you: do this and do not do that? No. Rather, He chooses for conveying His message whoever He selects from among the messengers: ﴿God chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind...﴾ [al-Hajj: 75].

He chose Gabriel from among the angels to be the trustworthy one of His revelation, and He chose from among mankind the messengers and prophets. Hence the branch of faith in God is that we believe in all of God's messengers, and that we treat them equally in honor.

I recall that one of the Orientalists asked me in San Francisco: "How do you permit a Muslim man to marry a Christian (kitabiyya) woman, but you do not permit a Christian man to marry a Muslim woman? Why did you not make it like food and drink?" I said to them: "Because the Muslim believes in the messenger of the Christian woman, whereas the Christian does not believe in the messenger of the one he wants to marry (the Muslim woman)."

His saying: ﴿and it is the truth from their Lord...﴾ [Muhammad: 2], meaning: what was sent down upon Muhammad is the truth, and the truth is the thing that is established and does not change or alter. Then comes the fruit of faith: ﴿He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition﴾ [Muhammad: 2].

Among God's mercy to His servants is that He prescribed repentance for them and opened for them the door of seeking forgiveness. He, glory be to Him, is their Creator and knows them best and what sets them right. He knows that man is by nature heedless.

Therefore He said: ﴿and He pardons much﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 15]. He also prescribed expiations (kaffarat) for us: prayer expiates for the prayer that follows it, Friday for the Friday that follows it, and Ramadan for the Ramadan that follows it. All of these are expiators of sins, as though they were sales (awkaziyonat) of forgiveness, so that we do not despair of God's mercy and do not persist in disobedience.

So forgiveness of sins is a mercy by which God shows mercy to His servants, so that they do not enter through the door of despair, and disobedience does not spread and take root among people.

His saying: ﴿and He set right their condition (bal)﴾ [Muhammad: 2]. All the exegetes say it means: He set right their whole condition, the psychological, moral and material. But there is a difference between bal and hal. The bal is, in reality, the thought that comes to the mind. You say: "This thing is on my mind (bali)," meaning it is in my intellect and never leaves me. A person usually occupies his mind with his current situation. A student, for example, occupies his mind with success and failure, the college and work after graduation. So whoever God sets right in his mind, his situation is set right.

﴿That﴾ refers to the reward mentioned earlier, the reward of the disbelievers whose deeds Allah has caused to go astray, and the reward of the believers whose misdeeds He has expiated and whose state He has set right. Here He explains the reason and cause for this. The disbelievers followed falsehood, and the believers followed truth. Falsehood is non-existent, while truth is manifest and enduring. Whoever follows that which does not exist finds every good absent from him, and whoever follows the enduring truth that exists finds every good present with him.

But why did the people of falsehood follow falsehood? They followed it because it imposes no obligations that restrain their desires, and it has no prohibitions at which they must stop. Falsehood gives the self free rein to plunge into its appetites, pleasures and desires.

Through falsehood a person steals and lives off the sweat, indeed the blood, of others. Through falsehood a person harbours spite towards another, envies him and kills him. Truth, however, prevents you from all of this and restrains in you every movement that contradicts the requirements of faith.

Otherwise, why were idols worshipped, and why were the sun, the moon and the stars worshipped? Yes, they know that these neither harm nor benefit, but they have no obligations that bind them, so they worshipped them.

As for the words of Allah, ﴿Thus Allah sets forth for people their parables﴾, the setting forth of parables (amthal, sing. mathal, "parable, illustrative example") is one of the forms of clarification in the Noble Qur'an, by which the meaning is made clear. On matters where understandings falter, Allah, glorified is He, clarifies them for people through a parable, to bring them closer to the minds.

Just as He set forth for us a parable concerning those who associate partners with Allah, saying, ﴿Allah sets forth a parable: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in comparison?..﴾ [al-Zumar: 29].

When you read this parable, the evil outcome of polytheism and the safety of monotheism become clear to you. They are opposites that are not equal, just as a slave belonging to several masters is not equal to one who belongs to a single master. Moreover, those masters are not in agreement with one another but at odds, so that he cannot please any of them, whereas the other is the slave of one single master.

And just as Allah set forth for us a parable of His light, or of His illuminating the universe, in Surat al-Nur: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is in a glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light..﴾ [al-Nur: 35].

Among the illustrative parables is: ﴿The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like the spider who takes a home; and indeed the frailest of homes is the spider's home, if only they knew.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 41].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks⟩ [Muhammad: 4]. That is, on the field of battle, when the millstone of war has turned between you. ﴿Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them⟩ [Muhammad: 4]. The infinitive "ḍarb" (striking) here carries the sense of the imperative: strike their necks.

What is meant is killing, whether by striking the necks or otherwise, but the striking of the necks is mentioned because it is the most emphatic form of killing. ﴿...Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them⟩ [Muhammad: 4]: that is, you have brought their movement to an end and weakened them so that they cannot resist. The root "thakhn" (ثخن) is the same as "takhun" (تخن), meaning that it became firm and heavy so that it no longer moves.

We understand this meaning when we consider, for example, the housewife who cooks rice with milk, or boils honey to make jam. With the boiling, the water evaporates and a thick, heavy substance remains, which therefore does not move as it boils, and its heat is intense. We say: "thakhuna al-shay'" or "takhuna."

﴿Then tighten the bonds⟩ [Muhammad: 4]: that is, bind them and tie them with chains and ropes, and make their bonds secure so that they remain prisoners in your hands and do not escape. This means that once you have gained control over them, you do not let them go.

﴿...Then either [release them] as a favour or [take] ransom⟩ [Muhammad: 4]. Either you release them and set them free (as a favour, "mann") without any compensation, or (as ransom, "fidā'") you take a ransom from them. But when? You release them without compensation in the case where they have left our captives with them without compensation, and you take ransom if they demand a ransom from us for our captives whom they hold.

This is what they call reciprocal treatment, and it is what the United Nations has now arrived at in such situations.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿...until the war lays down its burdens⟩ [Muhammad: 4]. "War" here is a metonym for its people and the parties involved in it. The meaning is: do this until the millstone of war stops, and "its burdens" means that they lay down the weights of war, for war is a burden and a hardship upon its people.

For this reason God said concerning it: ﴿Fighting has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you⟩ [al-Baqarah: 216]. Indeed, in war you are exposed to losing your property, losing your family, and losing your very life, besides its hardships and difficulties: the advancing and retreating, the striking and wounding, etc.

﴿And had God willed, He could have defeated them⟩ [Muhammad: 4]: He would have overcome them and taken vengeance upon them by His power and without fighting by you. This is a matter that is easy for God, as happened to the earlier nations, whom God destroyed with a punishment from Him and with His might, which is not turned back from the disbelieving people. So this is not something strange; rather, it is a reality that history attests.

And recite: ﴿So each [of them] We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned⟩ [al-'Ankabut: 40].

So why was fighting prescribed, though it is hateful and involves hardship? God says: ﴿Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14].

So fighting was prescribed to demonstrate the strength of the believers, and then to test their faith and their steadfastness upon the truth, and to distinguish the believers from the hypocrites: ﴿But that He may test some of you by means of others⟩ [Muhammad: 4].

That is, He tests the believers through the disbelievers and the disbelievers through the believers, so that the faith of the believer may be purified, for he is the bearer of a message and of a method, and he will bear the responsibility of the call, travelling with it through all parts of the earth. Therefore it was necessary that he be refined, so that the bad might be distinguished from the good.

Who will endure the pains of war and stand firm and not flee, who will sacrifice his wealth and his self? God, when He tests, tests not so that He Himself may know, for He knows everything, but so that we may know, and so that the excellence of this nation and of this message may become manifest, and the greatness of this final Prophet who was sent to all people, in every age and every place.

Its followers must necessarily be equal to this responsibility and worthy of bearing the burdens of the message after our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

It is related that our master Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr was the pampered youth of Quraysh, who would go out and come back several times, each time in a new garment, its fragrance of many kinds. When he embraced Islam his condition changed, and the Messenger of God sent him to Madinah to teach the people. He wore coarse clothing and renounced the luxury of worldly delights he had enjoyed.

When his mother learned of his state, she grieved over him, refused food, and sat in the heat of the sun to turn her son away from what he was in and bring him back to the religion of the fathers and grandfathers. When Mus'ab learned of his mother's conduct, he said to them: "Tell my mother: By God, if she had a hundred souls and they left her one by one, I would not abandon this religion. Leave her; if hunger bites her, she will eat, and if the heat of the sun burns her, she will seek shade."

Mus'ab remained in Madinah until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came, and he saw him wearing a sheepskin, and [the Prophet] said: ...

So: war in Islam is for a wisdom. It is like the fire that removes the impurities from gold and iron so that it becomes firm. For this reason God prepared this nation to be a nation of fighting and bravery even before His Messenger (ﷺ) was sent.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was compelled to fight, he did not train soldiers, nor did he open a military college; rather, he found men skilled in the arts of fighting, because the wars that broke out between the tribes and continued for a period reaching forty years made this nation an army on constant readiness, so that whenever they heard a cry of alarm they flew toward it.

Moreover, it was a Bedouin nation living on migration, their houses on the backs of camels, following the places where rain falls and the grass grows, as though God, may He be exalted, was preparing them to bear this message.

﴿And those who are killed in the way of God—He will never waste their deeds⟩ [Muhammad: 4]. Those who are killed in the way of God are the martyrs. ﴿He will never waste their deeds⟩ [Muhammad: 4]: He will not nullify them, but will pay them their rewards and recompense them for them, because the martyr has given his life to God and sacrificed the most precious thing he possesses in the way of God. Therefore He rewards him with honour and favour beyond what occurs to his mind.

He rewards him by the principle: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it⟩ [al-Nisa': 86]. Because he gave himself generously in the way of God, God frees him from death a second time. So his life is joined to the life of the Hereafter: the martyr, after being killed in this world, becomes alive with God until he is raised in that life in the Hereafter.

The Arab poet noticed this meaning when praising Hamzah, lord of the martyrs, saying:

O Hamzah, paternal uncle of the Chosen One, and lord of all the martyrs entire,
And it suffices you of that martyrdom a protection from death, in joining the two lives to the other.

So those who object to the life of the martyr and say: "If we opened the grave of a martyr, would we find him alive?" No, you would find him dead. But this is a narrow view of the question of life and death. To set your mind at ease, recite: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for⟩ [Al 'Imran: 169].

Consider the words ﴿with their Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169], and He did not say "with you." Rather, they are alive with their Lord, with a life that none knows but Him, may He be glorified. This is one of the unseen matters that must be accepted: he is alive with his Lord, even if he is dead in your sight.

Then His saying ﴿they are provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169] is another proof of his life, because provision is among the means of sustaining life.

How could He guide them when they are already guided? Those who were martyred were only killed while they were guided. So the guidance here is of the kind in His words: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. It means He guides them to Paradise, or to acknowledging His favour and thanking Him for His blessing.

For this reason He relates of the people of Paradise: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us"﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. And He says of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions and what they used to worship, besides Allah, and lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 22–23].

So these are guided to bliss, and those are guided to Hellfire.

Through this guidance the martyr recognises his palace in Paradise without any address. No one has to point it out to him; he knows it. This is why He, glorified is He, says afterwards: ﴿He will set right their condition and admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad: 5–6]. The meaning of ﴿He will set right their condition﴾ [Muhammad: 5] is: He will set right their state of mind (bal), that is, their concerns and inner state.

So the guidance here is of the kind in His words: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. It means He guides them to Paradise, or to acknowledging His favour and thanking Him for His blessing.
