The meaning of ﴿He will set right their condition﴾ [Muhammad: 5] is: He will set right their state of mind (bal), that is, their concerns and inner state.

This is a battle-related matter for the Muslims, a fact that does not fail and a principle that does not waver, and one of God's laws that does not change as long as the condition of soldiership is upheld for God and for the support of God's religion.

Therefore we have said: if you see the Muslims defeated in a battle, know that they have not fulfilled the condition of soldiership for God, and investigate among them the cause of the defeat, because God's law regarding the support of the faithful group is a established law.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ [As-Saffat: 171-173] Thus we saw what happened at the Battle of Uhud when the archers disobeyed the orders of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and went out of the condition of soldiership.

Likewise was the case on the Day of Hunayn, about which God said: ﴿And [recall] the Day of Hunayn, when your large number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with all its vastness; then you turned back, fleeing.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 25]

Even as-Siddiq himself was not spared the feelings of admiration for the enemy, so he said: "We will not be defeated today because of few numbers." When they were overcome by conceit in their numbers and admiration for their multitude, defeat befell them at the beginning.

But the mercy of God overtook them, and they were victorious at the end of the battle. It was as if it were a discipline from God to His faithful servants and a practical lesson, so that they would enter war with nothing in their minds but God and the support of God's religion.

And His saying: ﴿and make firm your feet﴾ [Muhammad: 7] – the firmness of the feet is a metaphor for steadfastness in battle and a metaphor for strength, because the feet are the means of fleeing from war; so when God makes them firm, they stand firm and do not flee. Therefore, the trust of the foot is that it not flee on the day of the advance.

This is the counterpart. After mentioning the believers and promising them victory, He mentioned the disbelievers and what befalls them of ruin. Ta's (ruin, stumbling) is being thrown down upon the face, which is the most noble part of a human being. Therefore, in expressing humiliation and abasement, they say: "He rubbed his nose in the dust."

So: ﴿So ruin for them...﴾ [Muhammad: 8] means: humiliation or destruction for them. Disgracing the face is the most severe way a person can be disgraced. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes, to disfigure your faces...﴾ [al-Isra: 7].

His saying: ﴿and He caused their deeds to go astray﴾ [Muhammad: 8] means He nullified and voided them, such that there is no benefit in them, because they did not do them for Allah.

The meaning is that their good deeds go to waste (haba'), and they gain nothing from them: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, so He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

That is an indication of the punishment of the disbelievers mentioned earlier, namely their stumbling and the nullification of their deeds: ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah has sent down﴾. This is the cause of the nullification of their deeds. But why did they dislike what Allah had sent down?

They disliked what Allah had sent down because the way of Allah would strip the carpet of dominion and arrogance from beneath their feet. It would make them equal to their slaves, after they had become accustomed to sovereignty, rank, and even domination over people. Therefore they disliked the truth when the Messenger of Allah brought it.

When our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), went to Madinah, they were preparing Abdullah ibn Ubayy to be crowned king over Madinah. But when the Messenger of Allah arrived, the people dispersed from him and busied themselves with the arrival of the Messenger of Allah. This remained in the soul of Abdullah, and he continued his hostility toward the Messenger. Even after he declared his Islam, he was not sincere in it, and he was a well-known hypocrite (munafiq) whose hypocrisy was famous.

Nevertheless, he had a son who embraced Islam and whose Islam was good, and who accompanied the Messenger of Allah. When this son learned that the Messenger of Allah had ordered the killing of this hypocrite, he came to the Messenger of Allah and asked him to permit him to kill him, so that another man from the Companions would not kill him and he would harbour something in his soul because of it. When he said this, the Messenger of Allah refused except to show mercy to him and to excuse him from this. He said: "Do not kill him, and defer him to Allah."

As for His saying ﴿so He has made their deeds fruitless﴾: we have said that it means He nullified them. Either it refers to their deeds, their plotting, and their scheming against the Muslims, by the Muslims' victory over them and by Allah turning their scheming back against them; or it means He nullified their good deeds, because they did not seek thereby the Face of Allah.

It is well known that among these people were some who had good deeds with weight in their society. It is related that Ibn Ju'dan and al-Mut'im ibn Adi had cooking pots for food, under whose shade a man could take shelter. They had renown for generosity, courage, relieving the distressed, and other things. But they did not do this for Allah, so it went as scattered dust.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 10:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth...﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. This is an interrogative whose purpose is to express wonder at the conduct of the disbelievers. How can they disbelieve in God when they are a people of travel and journeys, who pass during their journeys by the remains of the dwellings of the nations that denied, and see what punishment befell them and how God seized them? Have they not taken a lesson from them!?

He, Exalted is He, said in another verse: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then use reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138]. And He said: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah judges; there is no repeal of His judgement, and He is swift in reckoning.﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].

And in another verse: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? Then are they the victors?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 44]. That is: take a lesson from the reality of life. Have you seen a messenger who was defeated before his opponents?

So: let them take a lesson from the earlier nations, ﴿so that they may look at how was the end of those before them...﴾ [Muhammad: 10], what God did to them. ﴿God destroyed them completely...﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. "Dammara" (destroyed completely) has a meaning: it means He ruined them in their very selves. The phrase "dammara 'alayhim" means: He ruined them and laid waste to them, and the punishment closed in upon them, so He destroyed them, destroyed their wealth and destroyed their families, and left nothing of theirs remaining.

﴿And for the disbelievers there are its like﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. That is: this fate is not far from you, O disbelievers of Makkah, so beware. As He said in another verse: ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 83].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That﴾ [Muhammad: 11], i.e., what occurred of God's retribution against the disbelievers, the deliverance of the believers, and their victory. ﴿Because God is the Protector (mawla) of those who believe﴾ [Muhammad: 11]: their Protector, meaning the One who helps them and takes charge of their affairs, and He, glory be to Him, is Mighty and cannot be overcome. ﴿And the disbelievers have no protector﴾ [Muhammad: 11], no helper and no supporter, because they worshipped gods that neither harm nor benefit.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 47, verse 12:

Almighty God here tells us about the deeds of the people of faith and their outcome, and the deeds of the people of disbelief and their outcome. The believer has cultivated his heart with faith, and his limbs have been cultivated with righteous deeds, so the outcome is ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow...﴾ [Muhammad: 12], where there is everlasting bliss that never runs out.

The meaning of ﴿beneath which...﴾ [Muhammad: 12] is that their water is inherent within them, abundantly available to them; it does not come to them from afar, and there is no fear of its cutting off.

As for the disbelievers, they eat and enjoy food and drink, filling with it their bellies and their bodies, while their hearts are empty and ruined, devoid of meanings and of faith.

Thus they live a life most resembling the life of animals and beasts: they have excess in material things, and poverty in meanings and values. This is their state in this world. Then comes the outcome and the natural recompense: ﴿And the Fire is their dwelling place﴾ [Muhammad: 12], meaning: their final destination, their place of return, their abode, and their destiny.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 13:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And how many a city⁠—﴾ [Muhammad: 13], meaning: many cities ﴿were mightier in strength than your city which has expelled you. We destroyed them, and there was none to help them﴾ [Muhammad: 13]. What is meant here is Makkah, for it is the one that expelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And where is it compared with the cities that Allah destroyed, which were mightier than it, more numerous, and more advanced in civilization and building?

As the Truth, glory be to Him, said about them: ﴿And have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength, and they tilled the earth and populated it more than these have populated it...﴾ [Ar-Rum: 9].

Where are they from ʿAd, who had no equal produced in the lands, and Thamud, who hewed the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh of the stakes (dhu al-Awtad)? Where are they from these destroyed ones? ﴿We destroyed them, and there was none to help them﴾ [Muhammad: 13], meaning there was no defender to ward off the punishment from them.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 47, verse 14:

God, glory be to Him, wishes to establish this truth, but He presents the matter in the form of a question: "Are those two equal?" ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord...﴾ [Muhammad: 14]. That is: upon guidance, upon proof, and upon light from his Lord.

The Rabb (Lord) is the Creator and the Nurturer, and consider how great the nurturing is when it comes from God. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ), in the context of explaining the favour of his Lord upon him, said: ...

The meaning of ﴿upon clear evidence...﴾ [Muhammad: 14] is: upon a clear matter, a firm certainty, and a straight method, which guarantees him good in this world and safety in the Hereafter. Is this equal to one whose evil deeds have been made attractive to him, and who follows his desires and passions? You will surely say: they are not equal.

Among the greatest trials into which a person falls is that his desire makes his evil deed appear good to him, so he sees it as fine. Hawa (desire) is the inclination and longing that turns you away from the straight path. For this reason they said: "The bane of opinion is desire." Accordingly, God, glory be to Him, praised His Prophet (ﷺ) by saying: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ [An-Najm: 3].

Then the context returns once more to the striking of parables, and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿The parable of the Garden which the righteous have been promised...⦆.

The word ﴿مَّثَلُ﴾ [Muhammad: 15] is said with a kasra on the mim (مِثل, *mithl*) when you liken one single thing to another single thing. You say: "This is *mithl* (like) that." It is said with a fatha on the mim (مَثَل, *mathal*) when you liken a picture that has parts to another picture that has parts. So here the Exalted says: ﴿The *mathal* (parable) of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised...﴾ [Muhammad: 15], with the mim opened, because it represents a whole and an overall image that has many elements and parts.

Read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The *mathal* of the life of this world...﴾ [al-Kahf: 45], that is, with all that it contains from birth to death: ﴿like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, then it becomes dry stubble that the winds scatter; and God is ever Able over everything﴾ [al-Kahf: 45].

The *mathal* (parable) is a comparison in which you attach something unknown to you to something known to you. Therefore, when our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), was asked about the descriptions of Sayyidina Musa and Sayyidina Isa (peace be upon them), he likened them to what was known to the Companions. He said: "As for Musa, he is a tall man, as if he were one of the men of Azd Shanu'a," which was well known to them. "As for Isa, he is abundant in *khilan* (moles/beauty marks) of the face," meaning that his face has many fine marks, "his face drips with water, as if he had come out of a *dimas*," meaning a bathhouse, "and the one most like him among my Companions is 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi." So, he likened the unknown to what is known.

Likewise, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck parables for us to clarify matters of religion, and he said in his hadith: ...

The word ﴿*al-Jannah*﴾ [Muhammad: 15] (the Garden) originally means the hidden thing, and from it comes *jinn* (the hidden beings) and *janna al-layl* (the night covered over with darkness). Even the garden of this world carries this meaning, because it is a piece of land full of trees with intertwined branches, such that it conceals what is in it, or it *yajunn* (covers over) its owner, meaning it shields him and prevents him from leaving it, since it provides him with all the requirements of his life.

The Exalted, glorified is He, struck a parable with it: ﴿Like the parable of a garden on a height: a heavy rain strikes it and it yields its produce twofold; and if a heavy rain does not strike it, then a light drizzle...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 265].

And He said: ﴿And present to them the parable of two men: We had made for one of them two gardens...﴾ [al-Kahf: 32].

The difference between the two gardens is that the garden of this world is made by human beings and by directly engaging in the means of tilling and planting, whereas the Garden of the Hereafter, which God promised to the God-fearing, stands without means, standing by the power of the One who causes causes. Therefore, a disagreement arose about the garden that Sayyidina Adam (peace be upon him) entered: was it the garden of this world, or the garden of the Hereafter?

When we read this story in the Book of God, we know that it was the Garden of God, the Garden of the Hereafter, as evidenced by the fact that he did not till in it or plant, and did not engage in means. Rather, he ate from what God had prepared for him, and he was in a state of self-sufficient security for the duration of his stay, while obeying God's command regarding eating.

When Satan seduced him to eat from the tree which God had forbidden him, a change occurred in the natural condition he had been in. He saw in himself the matter of expulsion, which he had not been accustomed to before, and he became aware of his nakedness and began to cover it with the leaves of trees, he and his wife.

This matter was a practical training for Adam in respecting the method and not deviating from it. We also understand likewise that nakedness does not appear in a Muslim society except when a deviation from the method occurs. Adam (peace be upon him) was not an ordinary man; rather, he was a prophet and messenger, so the Exalted wished to teach him the lesson in a practical way.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿...that the God-fearing have been promised...﴾ [Muhammad: 15], that is, God promised them it, and the promise of God is true and binding, because He is one God with no partner opposing Him, and no power stands between Him, glorified is He, and the execution of what He has promised, as happens, for example, in the promises of human beings to one another, because change befalls human beings and death overtakes them.

As for the Exalted, He is the Everlasting, the Abiding, and He is the Truth.

The Garden is God's promise, and no one else promises it. Whom does He promise it to? He promises it to the God-fearing (*al-muttaqun*), and the God-fearing person is the one who walks according to God's method and places between himself and the punishment of God a shield, and this is achieved only by following the method and not following Satan and whims.

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty; and God is All-Encompassing, Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 268].

The promise of God is a promise of truth and a promise of reality. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who is more truthful than God in statement?﴾ [al-Nisa: 122].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The *mathal* of the Garden...﴾ [Muhammad: 15] means that this description is not a description of the Garden itself, but a parable that brings it closer to minds, because if He wished to give us a description of the Garden in its reality, He would not reach that except through words that express meanings.

It is known in the language that the meaning exists first, then we place for it the word that indicates it. When the Prophet (ﷺ) described the Garden to us, he said, first: Reflect on this hadith's progression through the senses and perceptions: the eye sees what is within the field of vision, the ear hears what you see and what others see, and broader than all this is what occurs to the mind or heart.

So if our perceptions do not reach what is in the Garden, and it does not even occur to our minds, how can we describe it, and how can we set for it words that express it?

Therefore, this is not a description of the reality of the Garden, but merely a parable that brings it near to our understanding. For this reason He, exalted is He, said about the Garden: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes...﴾ [al-Sajdah: 17].

So, in it there are things we do not know, so how can we give them names? Therefore, we bring it near through a parable from what we know in this world.

In it, as in this world, there is water, milk, wine, and honey, but it is refined and purified from everything that mixes with it, so its bounties resemble the bounties of this world only in names: ﴿therein are rivers of water unaltered...﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

The water of this world becomes stagnant and putrid, and its smell changes, whereas the water of the Garden is water unaltered (*ghayr asin*). He began with water because it is the basis of quenching thirst, with it food is cooked, with it a person is cleansed, and indeed it is an essential element in the creation of every living being. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing...﴾ [al-Anbiya: 30].

We know that the source of sweet water in this world is the seas, and through evaporation and the formation of clouds it is purified from saltiness and becomes sweet and fit for use. But the water of the Garden, we do not know its source.

He said of it: ﴿pure water﴾ [al-Furqan: 48], not tainted by any stain, and no pollutants reach it to spoil it. So it is a blessing that nothing spoils and no impurity mixes with it, because in this world you live by your means which God created for you.

Among us are those who disturb the serenity of these means, whereas in the Hereafter you live directly by the One who causes causes, glorified is He. In this world you are illuminated by the sun by day, and by the moon and stars by night, but in the Hereafter there is no sun, no moon, and no stars; rather, you live by the light of God: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord...﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], that is, without means.

Likewise, you take water in this world by means, and in the Garden without means. Read His saying about water in this world: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing, then We sent down water from the sky and gave it to you to drink...﴾ [al-Hijr: 22].

And He said about the water of the Garden: ﴿And their Lord gave them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21].

There is a difference in meaning between (*asqa*) and (*saqa*). *Asqa*: it creates the water from which we draw when we want watering; the water descends from the clouds, and we hold it behind dams until we need it. But (*saqa*) actually undertakes the act of watering.

Among the wonders of the rivers of the Garden is that they have no banks, and that they flow intertwined without some of them mixing with others. Do not ask here about how that is, because this bounty does not stand on the means we know, but on the One who causes causes, glorified is He, so you should not judge it by your judgment of its like in this world. His saying ﴿therein...﴾ [Muhammad: 15] means that it is the container of these rivers.

﴿And rivers of milk, whose taste never changes...﴾ [Muhammad: 15], whereas the milk of this world changes in taste over time and spoils. ﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink...﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. Yes, rivers of wine, prepared and ready, with no grapes being pressed; rather, by "Be, and it is."

If the wine of this world is forbidden, and it takes away the intellect and has a foul smell, the wine of the Hereafter has pleasure when drunk and does not take away the intellect, so it has from the wine of this world only its name.

There are no rivers of wine in this world, because the wine of this world is made through means; it comes in small quantities, in proportion to what is pressed from grapes or other things. When the Exalted spoke about the wine of this world He said: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both is great sin and benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219].

Benefits have no value when compared with harms and prohibition. It is true that they make you feel some euphoria or happiness, you laugh, rejoice, and forget your worries, but afterward they assassinate your intellect and rob you of your dignity.

If you add to that that it is prohibited, and that it is among the greatest of the major sins (*al-kaba'ir*), its harm becomes clear to you. It is true that there is profit for whoever trades in it, but it is unlawful profit. Therefore God made the wine of this world scarce, whereas the wine of the Hereafter comes in rivers, because in the Hereafter it is a delight for those who drink.

﴿No intoxication is in it, nor are they drained by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47], that is, it does not assassinate the intellect, and no harm results from drinking it. *Al-naz*f is the removal of something from something, like someone who vomits after drinking it, or is afflicted with dizziness or headache.

﴿And rivers of honey, pure...﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. So he mentioned water first because of its primary importance, then milk, because it carries the role of water until water is present, and it is an essential element of nourishment. Then he mentioned wine, because after eating and drinking a person needs, for complete happiness, a cup of this wine.

As for honey, it comes at the end of this list, because God, exalted is He, said of it: ﴿In it is healing for people...﴾ [al-Nahl: 69]. So the distinguishing feature of honey is not in its taste and sweetness, but in its being a cure, and there is no sickness in the Garden. Therefore, in the Garden it is drunk for its delight and the beauty of its taste.

The meaning of ﴿*musaffa*﴾ [Muhammad: 15] (purified) is to distinguish it from the honey of this world, which is never free of impurities, because people gather it from the mountains, which are the first pasture of the bees: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee: take houses in the mountains, and in trees, and in what they construct﴾ [al-Nahl: 68].

An American researcher who studied the life of bees found that mountain bees are the oldest kind of bees. And since it comes from the mountains, it is never free of impurities, whereas the honey of the Garden is purified by the power of the One who prepared it, glorified is He.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And for them therein is every kind of fruit...﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. After the Exalted mentioned what is in the Garden of liquids, He mentions what is in it of fruits without naming them, because we do not know them.

For this reason He said in another verse: ﴿and they will be given something similar in appearance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25], meaning fruits that are similar in appearance but differ in taste. Even when He gave us an example with grapes and general terms, what is in the Garden is other than what we know in this world.

If fruits in our world have environments in which they flourish and have seasons, the fruits of the Garden are present at all times. The environments of this world are among the means, whereas the Hereafter is by the One who causes causes, glorified is He.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And forgiveness from their Lord...﴾ [Muhammad: 15], after our Lord, glorified is He, has given us the pleasure of matter and form in the Garden, He gives us a higher pleasure, which is the pleasure of obtaining forgiveness from God out of generosity and bounty, because they did not enter the Garden except by forgiveness. Yet one of them may mention his sin, and He says to him: "You are forgiven."

It has been reported in the hadith qudsi (sacred hadith) that after the people of the Garden enter the Garden, the Lord of Might, glorified is He, asks them: ...

Then the Exalted places us before this comparison between the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire. He says: ﴿Is one who abides eternally in the Fire, and is given boiling water to drink which cuts their bowels to pieces?﴾ [Muhammad: 15], meaning: which of them is better? Judge for yourself, and we will accept your judgment.

This is the Garden, or a parable of it: can it be equal to its opposite, the one who abides eternally in the Fire? ﴿and is given boiling water to drink which cuts their bowels to pieces﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. Just as water was mentioned first in the Garden, it is also mentioned first in the Fire, God forbid.

The word ﴿*wa-suqu*﴾ [Muhammad: 15] (and they are given to drink), and not "they drank," because drinking is voluntary and by choice, whereas ﴿*suqu*﴾ means against their will and without their wish, like when you give a small child medicine and make him drink it, unwillingly.

﴿boiling water﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. Water is known to be drunk to quench thirst, and drunk cold. But the water of Hell, God forbid, is *hamim*, meaning its heat has reached its extreme. How will they be, while they are in the Fire and want to cool the heat of their insides, but they are given to drink *hamim*, which increases their heat above the heat of the Fire?

Therefore He, exalted is He, said in another verse: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal that scorches faces﴾ [al-Kahf: 29].

Then He explains the effect of this boiling water: ﴿which cuts their bowels to pieces﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. Would that it cut them and the matter ended! Rather, they are in a lasting, constant punishment that is never lightened for them. ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment...﴾ [al-Nisa: 56]. *Al-amʻa'* is the plural of *mi'an* (intestine), with a kasra on the mim. The noble hadith has also been transmitted with the saying of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ...

Meaning: the believer eats according to his need, or in his eating and in his food there is blessing, whereas the disbeliever eats until his belly is filled.

**The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And among them﴾ [Muhammad: 16]. Who are "them"? You will know after you read their description: ﴿those who listen to you﴾ [Muhammad: 16], listening to the Messenger of Allah as he recites the Qur'an, ﴿until, when they go out from your presence﴾ [Muhammad: 16], O Muhammad, ﴿they say to those who have been given knowledge﴾ [Muhammad: 16], such as Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿"What did he just say?"﴾ [Muhammad: 16], meaning: what is new in what Muhammad has said? As if they belittle what they have heard from the Messenger of Allah.**

**These, then, are not the attributes of the disbelievers, because the disbelievers did not listen to the Qur'an. Rather, they are the attributes of the hypocrites (munafiqun), who used to join the Muslims in their prayers and their gatherings, and who blended in among them with malice and cunning. But the Qur'an was descending upon the Messenger of Allah and exposing them.**

**For this reason, hypocrisy (nifaq) was worse and more harmful to the Muslims than disbelief (kufr). The disbelievers are known to be an open enemy, and one can guard against them. As for the hypocrite, he is one of the Muslim community who professes Islam and conceals disbelief, so his enmity is not apparent, and his danger is greater.**

**Whoever traces the history of hypocrisy in Islam finds that it did not appear in Makkah but appeared in Madinah. Despite the intense hostility between Islam and the disbelievers in Makkah, it was an open, declared enmity that could be confronted. Hypocrisy did not exist there; it appeared only in Madinah. Why?**

**Because hypocrisy occurs only with the strong. The weak does not feign friendship toward the weak; you declare enmity to his face. But the strong, you feign friendship toward him in order to overcome him.**

**So what is the reason for hypocrisy in Makkah when the Muslims there were a small, oppressed minority? This means that hypocrisy is a phenomenon that indicates the strength of faith, and that it had become a power that must be flattered, and this happened in Madinah.**

**For this reason, He, glorified and exalted, said about them: ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who have become hardened in hypocrisy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101].**

**The word ﴿yastami'u﴾ [Muhammad: 16]. This root occurs in the Qur'an in the forms: sami'a, istama'a, and tasamma'a. Sami'a means to hear without intending to listen. Istama'a means to listen to someone who wishes to hear something beloved to him. As for tasamma', it contains effort and deliberate striving to hear.**

**So He said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ [Muhammad: 16], meaning: by their own desire and will, and while they love to hear. This was the state of the hypocrites: they would sit in the front rows and show a concern that others did not show. No word would escape them, and no prayer would escape them, so that they could weave their plot and conceal their hypocrisy.**

**﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ [Muhammad: 16], because they heard the speech but did not believe in it, nor did they act in accordance with its requirements. So the recompense was that Allah sealed their hearts and stamped upon them. It is as if Allah is saying to them: Since you have loved hypocrisy, I will increase you in it, and I will seal your hearts so that hypocrisy does not leave them and faith does not enter them.**

**﴿And they followed their desires﴾ [Muhammad: 16]. Hawa (desire) is when your heart inclines toward something you believe to be pleasing and delightful to you: a quick joy and a momentary pleasure, without considering the consequences that follow this pleasure.**

**So: set boundaries for your desire, and choose the desire that leaves the more lasting effect and the more enduring benefit. Make your desire lie in what benefits you, not in what harms you. Consider the one who eats hot pepper (shatta), for example. It gives the eating a pleasure and a taste that he desires at the moment he eats, but he has overlooked the matter of its passing through him, and that it will bring upon him a pain that exceeds the pleasure of eating.**

**So: the sensible person must reflect on the consequences of his desire and beware lest desire carry him away. For this reason, the Exalted says: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 71].**

**The Truth, glorified is He, has brought us the method (manhaj) to protect us from desire, because the desires of souls are conflicting and opposed. They are a means of disagreement and discord, and Allah wants us to be united, and to support one another, not to oppose one another.**

**In a noble hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) says: Some people stop at His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ [Muhammad: 16], and say: since Allah sealed their hearts and willed for them to be misguided, why does He punish them? We say: Allah guides the servants; He does not misguide them. It is they who choose misguidance and do not become guided by faith.**

**For this reason, we read: ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264], and ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 108], and ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 258].**

**So misguidance and the absence of guidance arise from them and as a result of their crooked path. Allah did not guide them because they are either disbelievers, or defiantly disobedient, or wrongdoers.**

**Otherwise, in reality, the Truth, glorified is He, has guided everyone, the believer and the disbeliever, because He called out to all of them in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿O mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21]. He thus indicated to all of them and guided them to His method and to the outcome of walking on this method, and He warned them of the outcome of deviating from it.**

**He also made clear to them that the method was set down only for their own benefit, for the order of their affairs in this world and their safety in the Hereafter. He, glorified is He, is not benefited by obedience, nor harmed by disobedience. He is free of need for them, independent of their worship, for He possesses the attributes of perfection before He created them. He says to His servant: O My servant, turn toward Me, and I will give you of My goodness.**

**Consider His saying regarding the people of Thamud: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾ [Fussilat: 17], meaning: We made them aware and guided them to the path of good ﴿but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17]. So when they preferred blindness, Allah blinded them.**

**Then, those who say: Why does Allah punish them when He has misguided them? Why do they not mention the counterpart? They say: since He has obligated them to obey, why does He reward them for it?**

**For this reason, a divine hadith (hadith qudsi) has been transmitted: [the text of the hadith is not included here]. We have previously illustrated the matter of guidance, and to Allah belongs the highest example, by the traffic policeman: when you go to him and ask him about the road, he says to you: The road is from here. If you obey him, he increases your guidance and tells you: There is an obstacle on the road at such-and-such a place, so be careful of it, or he takes you himself until you reach what you want.**

**Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, has pointed out the way to everyone and guided everyone. Whoever hears and obeys, guidance increases for him, and whoever turns away and rebels, misguidance increases for him by having his heart sealed.**

**For this reason, the scholars divided guidance into two types: the guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalalah), which is for both the believer and the disbeliever, and the guidance of divine success and assistance (hidayat al-tawfiq wa al-ma'unah), which is specific to the believer. Therefore, He said in the verse after it:**

**﴿And those who were guided, He increases them in guidance...﴾ [Muhammad: 17].**

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He increases those who are guided in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17], meaning: by granting them success and assistance in obedience. ﴿And He gives them their taqwa﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. It is as if taqwa is what comes to them, not that they go to it. He facilitates it for them and makes it beloved to them. Yet some think that obligation (taklif) is a burden upon the self and a fetter that restricts it. Not at all!

The one who reflects finds in obligation rest and tranquility for the self and the mind. Obligation is a protection for the self and a shield for it from ruin. Therefore, consider for example: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5].

The meaning of ﴿upon guidance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5] is that guidance is their mount to the goal they intend. It is therefore not a burden on the servant, for the Creator, glorified is He, never obligated us with what we cannot bear, and He did not make us servants except for our own benefit, in the order of this world and the safety of the next.

For this reason we have said: servitude to other than God is humiliation and disgrace, while servitude to God is might and honor. Servitude to people gives the master the best of his servant, but servitude to God gives you the best of God.

When the servant understands worship in this sense, he loves it, longs for it, and finds in it a pleasure that nothing else can rival. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Bilal, his muezzin: "Call to prayer, O Bilal, and give us rest with it." (Note: the hadith text as given in the commentary is cited here as it stands, with the phrase "أي: بالصلاة" rendered as "i.e., with the prayer," so the sentence reads:) Therefore, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Bilal, his muezzin, i.e., with the prayer: how easy and light it is on the heart of the believer, and how heavy it is on the heart of the hypocrite.

So: from guidance is that you pray as the common people pray, and from the increase of guidance is that you long for prayer, await it, and find your rest in it, because you are in the presence of your Lord, mighty and majestic. God is unseen, and He also amends His servant through the unseen, so prayer reforms you and reforms your condition from where you do not know.

Among the fruits of taqwa is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion (furqan), remove from you your misdeeds, and forgive you. And God is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Anfal: 29].

Whoever fears God, by virtue of the criterion that came to him from God, which is the Qur'an, He increases it, by making for him another criterion specific to him, a criterion that guides him, illuminates the path for him, and by which he distinguishes between things.

So: regarding the matter of taqwa, you need only walk toward it, intending to act and obey, and then you will find that it is the one that seeks you out and pursues you.

The discussion here concerns the disbelievers who pay no heed to the evidences of God's existence in the universe, nor to the miracles of the messengers so as to believe in them and affirm them, nor to God's rulings so as to act upon them. What are these people waiting for?

﴿Then do they await anything but the Hour...﴾ [Muhammad: 18], meaning: they are waiting for ﴿the Hour...﴾ [Muhammad: 18]. The Hour, for them, means death, because for a person time ends with death. Whoever dies, his resurrection has come. A person does not know his term or when he will die, for Allah has concealed it and kept it to Himself, glorified is He, so no one can know it.

So, the length of life and its brevity are not in our hands and we have no control over them, because they are left to the One in whose hand are lives and terms. But its breadth is in your hands, by occupying your life with righteous deeds, widening the circle of good in your life, and benefiting others. You can also add another dimension to your life, by doing good that remains as a memory of you after your death and as a store for you with your Lord.

When you know that life is a breath that enters and does not return, or a blink of an eye that does not come back, you should be on guard lest you die in disobedience to Allah, on guard lest you delay repentance or procrastinate in it, because you cannot guarantee when death will overtake you.

So when you hear the call to prayer, rise and answer the call. Do not say, "The time is long, and I will pray later." If you have money and are able to perform the pilgrimage, do not say, "I will perform Hajj next year," for if you cannot guarantee your life for a moment, how can you guarantee it after a year? It is true that there is no punishment for delaying these acts, but by delaying you lose the excellence of praying on time and the excellence of congregational prayer.

Therefore, a noble hadith has been reported. Some people understood "Work for your worldly life" [a saying] to mean: [work for] what suffices you throughout your life. But the meaning of work here is: work for the world at your own pace and do not become absorbed in it, and what escapes you of it today you will reach tomorrow. That is, take it slowly and do not take the matter from the first deal.

What is blameworthy in striving for the world is that the world takes over all your concern, takes all your time, and you want it in haste. More dangerous than that is that we use blessings and wealth to commit disobedience, or promote a commodity that is legally forbidden, so that the blessing in our hands turns into a calamity.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude...?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28], like many of our daughters today, whom we see half-dressed and naked, displaying the beauty Allah has bestowed upon them. Instead of being thankful for the blessing by preserving it, they deny it by displaying themselves.

Would that the one who strays only strayed in himself! What is more grievous than his straying is that he becomes an example for others, so that temptation spreads in society. Therefore He, exalted is He, says in the continuation of the verse: ﴿and caused their people to alight at the abode of ruin?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]. What is the abode of ruin? ﴿Hell, they will burn therein, and wretched is the settling place﴾ [Ibrahim: 29].

These temptations sweep over young people, especially in the stage of adolescence and when there is no opportunity for work, while they are still dependent on their families. So we say to our daughters: fear Allah! The young man is excused, a poor fellow; it is enough for him to fend off the raging of adolescence. Do not inflame in him a new raging by your display, your unveiling, and your lack of modesty.

I recall once that they wanted to honour one of their prominent men, so they held a party for him and brought in dancers and the like. I said, "Glory be to Allah! Is this how prominent men are honoured among us?" Then I took hold of our friend and said to him, "Oh, how sweet the dancing was tonight! The girl was loosening herself with piety and swaying with devotion!!" What exactly is your story?

Yes: ﴿and caused their people to alight at the abode of ruin﴾ [Ibrahim: 28].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that it come upon them suddenly...﴾ [Muhammad: 18], meaning: unexpectedly, ﴿for its signs have already come...﴾ [Muhammad: 18], that is, its signs (asbab/ashrat, the portents of the Hour), its distinctive marks that announce its nearness. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has told us some of these signs, saying: "True, the head in the shape of (I don't know what), and the lips have been reddened, and the eyebrows have been thinned..." etc. They change the creation of Allah and use the blessing of Allah to disobey Allah, and this is among the signs of the Hour.

Therefore we ask Allah to guide our daughters, to preserve each of them in her beauty, to make thanking Allah for the blessing an act of obedience to Him, glorified is He, and not to let the blessing Allah has given her be poisoned by disobedience to Him. And I say to guardians: fear Allah regarding your daughters, and do not compel them to work in indecent advertisements, for they are forbidden, and whoever eats from them is eating unlawful gain from what is forbidden.

Likewise, among the signs of the Hour which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed of, and said: and other signs.

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then how will they have their reminder when it has come to them?﴾ [Muhammad: 18], meaning: how or from where will they have remembrance, when its time has passed and the Resurrection has overtaken them? How will they have remembrance, and how will they begin a righteous deed again?

Then He concludes it with the matter of matters, which if it is sound, everything in a person is sound. So He says:

﴿So know that there is no god except Allah...﴾

﴿So know that there is no god but Allah..﴾ [Muhammad: 19]: Do not seek any means for anything other than Allah, and it is not permissible for you to turn to anyone other than Allah, for seeking refuge in other than Allah benefits nothing. His words ﴿So know..﴾ [Muhammad: 19] refer to knowledge, which is of three kinds: knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin), when one who is trustworthy in his truthfulness informs you of it; the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqin), when you see it with your own eyes and see its effect; and the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin), when you experience it yourself.

When the Truthful, glorified is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿So know that there is no god but Allah..﴾ [Muhammad: 19], does this mean that he does not know it? No, rather the meaning is: persist in it. Just as you knew it in the past, make it your state in the present and in the future. This is of the same kind as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, believe..﴾ [al-Nisa: 136], where He commands them to believe while He has already called them to it.

They said: If Allah commands something that already exists in the one commanded, the meaning is to persist in it. You are a believer, but you are required to persist in your faith in the future.

When the Truthful, glorified is He, commands His Prophet with this command, it is only to reassure him that if he is denied, opposed, and harmed in every kind of harm and mockery, he should not grieve or be concerned, because Allah is beside him, supporting him and strengthening him, and however much people may act, they will not prevent him from carrying out his call.

The sunnah (established way) of Allah regarding the messengers is that He grants them victory: ﴿And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the victorious. And indeed, Our soldiers, they will be the overcomers.﴾ [al-Saffat: 171-173]. Therefore we have said: If you see a soldier who claims to belong to Islam being defeated, know that the conditions of soldiership have failed in him; otherwise he would not have been defeated.

We took as an example what happened to the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud, when they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah and were defeated while he was among them. This is the sunnah of Allah, and you will not find any change in the sunnah of Allah. Had they achieved victory after disobeying the Messenger's command, his command would have become easy for them thereafter, and they would have said to themselves: We disobeyed him and we were victorious.

So, the defeat came to bring them back to what is right and to awaken their heedlessness regarding obedience to the command of the Messenger of Allah.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women..﴾ [Muhammad: 19]. Does this mean that the Messenger has a sin for which he must seek forgiveness? This is one of the matters around which much debate has revolved. The meaning here is: if your soul becomes forgetful and you commit a sin, then seek forgiveness, not that he had actually sinned. His Lord says to him: If a sin occurs from you, then seek forgiveness for it. Likewise, seek forgiveness for the believing men and believing women.

In another verse, the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what will follow..﴾ [al-Fath: 1-2]. Here He mentions a sin in regard to the Messenger, despite his being protected from sin (maʿsum). When the scholars examined such verses, they said: they belong to the category of: "The good deeds of the righteous (al-abrar) are the sins of those brought near (al-muqarrabun)."

It is well known that those brought near are at a higher level of obedience and compliance with Allah than the righteous, because the righteous are those who obey Allah, do good deeds, and carry out the commands.

As for those brought near, they go beyond that in drawing near to Allah. Even in the custom of people, the one close to you is the constant companion who does not leave you, who loves you, and who fears for you.

Likewise, the one brought near to Allah has a different law in dealing with Him from the law of the righteous, and a different measure of good and bad deeds that suits the degree of his nearness to his Lord, mighty and majestic.

Consider: if, for example, you fell ill, God forbid, and one of your acquaintances came to visit you during your illness, even once, what would you do? You would thank him and consider that he had fulfilled his duty.

But if your close friend visited you only once, what would you do? You would reproach and blame him, because you were expecting more from him than one visit. This is the meaning of: "The good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near."

So, a good deed from an ordinary person may be considered a sin in relation to the Prophet, because the Prophet is brought near, and for the one brought near there is a different reckoning, and this nearness has a price. Allah says to you: Maintain this degree of nearness to Me, and beware lest anything, even something small, occur from you that would be insignificant for others.

Or, as our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: His saying "(on behalf of my community)" means that he is not included in this ruling, so the forgetfulness that is permissible for others is not permissible for him, and forgetfulness on his part is therefore counted as a sin.

Observe the greatness of the Companion in the question, the greatness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the reply, and the greatness of the faith that trained these people.

So, it is possible for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to forget, and his forgetting is counted as a sin. Why? Because he is a messenger and a bearer of a message, charged with conveying it, and the lights of prophethood never leave him, so how could he forget? Therefore, when a common man asked the scholar-worshipper who was devoted to Allah, saying: What is the ruling on one who forgets in prayer? He said to him: Is it according to us or according to you? He said: Rather, according to us. He said: He performs the prostration of forgetfulness. He said: And according to you? He said: We kill him.

Why go far when the story of the disobedience of our father Adam (peace be upon him) is known to all? The Exalted says, regarding Adam: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and he erred.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 121]. So He called Adam's forgetting a disobedience. Why?

They said: Because Adam was created by Allah directly; Allah created him with His own hand and breathed into him of His spirit, so he has a distinction in creation that others do not have. And he was not charged except with one obligation, which is not to eat from the tree. So what would he forget and what would he remember, when it is one command?

Therefore, forgetting was a disobedience on his part, because he was a prophet and messenger, and he was the father of mankind. So the disobedience of Adam came for a wisdom, because he is the father of mankind, and mankind is of two kinds: protected from sin (maʿsum) and not protected from sin. The protected are the messengers, and the not protected are the rest of creation. So both kinds must be represented in Adam.

Thus, when the Truthful, glorified is He, addresses His Prophet (ﷺ) and says to him: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin..﴾ [Muhammad: 19], that is: for the forgetfulness that I have overlooked for your community, you seek forgiveness for it yourself, because it is not forgiven for you as it is forgiven for your community.

Then look at the instances in which Allah reproached His Prophet Muhammad. Read, for example: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1]. Merely because one of your wives became angry about something you had forbidden yourself, though Allah had made it lawful for you, this was counted as a sin.

Likewise, when he gave permission to some Companions to remain behind from fighting, his Lord reproached him: ﴿Allah pardon you! Why did you give them permission until those who were truthful became clear to you and you knew the liars?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43]. So He reproached him for that, but began by pardoning him.

Furthermore, the Messenger has two aspects: the aspect of humanity and the aspect of the message. Adam (peace be upon him) disobeyed through his humanity, as evidenced by the Exalted's saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and he erred. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 121-122]. So the message did not come to him until after he had undergone this experience, and he did what humans do; then his Lord chose him with the message.

When we reflect on the matters for which Allah reproached His Prophet Muhammad, we find that they are general matters in which there is no text or legal ruling that the Messenger of Allah contravened. He would exercise his own judgment in them as a human being, as the situation dictated.

For example, in the story of Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, for whose sake Allah reproached His Messenger, when He said: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him.﴾ [ʿAbasa: 1-2]. You find that this reproach is not an objection to what the Messenger of Allah did, but rather mercy towards him and compassion for him.

Because he turned away from Abdullah, who was a believer who had come to ask him about a ruling of the Sharia, in order to devote himself to some of the chiefs of disbelief. He (ﷺ), with his human reasoning, was eager for the guidance of these people, whereas Abdullah was a believer by nature.

So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was exerting himself on his own behalf in the cause of his call. Then read to the end of the story: ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him. As for one who considers himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention. And not upon you is it that he should not purify himself. But as for he who came to you striving, and he fears [Allah], from him you are distracted.﴾ [ʿAbasa: 3-10].

It is as if the Truthful, glorified is He, is saying to His Prophet: O Muhammad, your task is not that people believe; your task is only to guide them and show them the way: ﴿Your duty is only to convey..﴾ [Ali ʿImran: 20]. And He addressed him in another place, saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe.﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 3].

In al-Kahf: ﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces if they do not believe in this message.﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]. That is: you have no duty except to convey. As for the matter of faith, I want them to be believers in their hearts, not merely in their outward form, by choice and not by compulsion.

And He said: ﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain bowed to it.﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 4]. That is: We would compel them to believe.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And Allah knows your movement and your resting place.﴾ [Muhammad: 19]. The meaning of ﴿your movement..﴾ [Muhammad: 19] is your going to your work and your striving across the vast expanses of the earth in search of provision. And ﴿your resting place﴾ [Muhammad: 19] is your return to your homes and your shelter, your beds at night.

The meaning is: He, glorified is He, knows all your conditions, and nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him. We have previously spoken about the virtue of striving through the earth's expanses and drawing out its good, because if you stay in your house you will only take the blessings of that one environment, whereas when you move across the various regions of the earth, you will find other kinds of blessings.

The Creator, glorified is He, has distributed His bounty across all His earth. Every land has its provision: the desert has its provision, and the cultivated land has its provision. There is no poor land and rich land, such that if you took a longitudinal section of the globe you would find in it the same blessings as in the other sections.

We used to think that the barren desert had no good in it, but now it is a source of abundant livelihood for its people, who endured the hardship of life there for long years.

Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and observe..﴾ [al-Naml: 69], and He says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and then observe..﴾ [al-Anʿam: 11], that is: reflect on what is in it of signs and lessons. A person travels and moves either for tourism or for seeking provision, and in both cases he should not neglect reflection and contemplation of the signs of the universe.

In another place the Exalted says: ﴿Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could emigrate therein?﴾ [al-Nisa: 97]. So taqallub (moving about, turning over) is leaving the place where one settles for a place where one does not settle, and this requires financial capacity, companionship, and strength. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Or He seizes them in their going back and forth, and they cannot escape.﴾ [al-Nahl: 46].

So taqallub is thus a sign of strength. The wealthy man is the one who travels every day to a place, moving across the regions of the earth, whereas the poor man stays in his place and does not leave it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 20:

The phrase ﴿Why has a surah not been sent down?﴾ When you hear the word (law, "if only"), it is as if it expresses a wish for something to happen. They wish that a surah would be sent down to the Messenger of Allah commanding them to fight. The surah did indeed come down, but it came down commanding them to patience, to bearing hardships, and to not confronting their enemies.

But everything has its appointed time. This means that the movement of the believer is governed by the commands of the Truth. The obstinacy of the disbelievers and their standing against the call does not mean that we should attack them and fight them on our own initiative; rather, we await the commands.

﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it⁠—﴾ that is, the fighting you desire. ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease⁠—﴾ that is, the hypocrites ﴿looking at you with the look of one who has fainted from death⁠—﴾ This is a simile, like the look of one fainting from death. That is: one who has fainted from fear and terror.

For the hypocrite, it is easy to go and pray with the congregation in the mosque, even to stand in the first row. But when the matter reaches fighting, the situation changes and what was hidden of hypocrisy is exposed.

﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down⁠—﴾ clear in its indication of the intended meaning ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one who has fainted from death⁠—﴾ It is said: Death has come to you, O one who abandons prayer. Shall I go to fight and lose myself?!

﴿So woe to them⁠—﴾ that is: it would be better for them (awlā) to obey the command and go out to fight. The scholars explained this verse and said: ﴿So woe to them⁠—﴾ meaning: destruction is for them, and this is a threat if they do not turn back from their hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Obedience [is due]..﴾ [Muhammad: 21]. After ﴿So woe to them﴾ [Muhammad: 20], it makes us turn our attention away from affirming their destruction, and we say: obedience from them to the command of Allah, and "a known word" is better than their position and better than their hypocrisy.

﴿So when the matter is resolved upon..﴾ [Muhammad: 21], meaning: it is determined and they gather their resolve for action, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when you have resolved, then rely upon Allah..﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 159]. But is it the matter that resolves, or its owner?

So here there is an intensification that made the matter itself a person who resolves, determines and binds itself to action. That is because the discussion here concerns fighting, and fighting is the hardest thing a person can bear, for it means either martyrdom or victory over the enemy. ﴿Say: Do you await for us except one of the two best things, while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Himself or at our hands? So wait; indeed, we are with you waiting.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 52].

So: ﴿So when the matter is resolved upon..﴾ [Muhammad: 21] is more eloquent in expressing the meaning than: "you resolved upon the matter," as if the matter itself were the one urging you, and the matter does not urge you unless there is much good for you in it. And is there anything better than martyrdom in the way of Allah?

The story of Mukhayriq the Jew is well known: after he declared his Islam, he was summoned to fight, so he went out and fought until he was killed, and he entered Paradise having not performed a single prostration to Allah.

Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said about him: "Indeed, he is..." — [Sahih] "Be eager for death and life will be granted to you," the eternal life with Allah in Paradise.

And His saying: ﴿But if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them﴾ [Muhammad: 21], meaning: if they had been true to Him in His commands and His method, it would have been better for them. The good here is the freedom from death afterward, because he gave his soul willingly in the way of Allah; so Allah granted him life with Him.

This is a question from God with "hal," and an expectation from God with "'asa." God does not ask in order to learn; He asks in order to establish a fact that has already occurred.

The word ('asa) is a verb that expresses hope, and what follows it is the thing hoped for. Hope applies to something loved that is expected to happen and is possible. It differs from wishing (tamanni), which concerns something loved that is impossible to attain, as in the poet's words:

*Ala layta al-shababa ya'udu yawman*
*fa-okhbirahu bi-ma fa'ala al-mashibu*

("Would that youth would return one day, so I could tell it what old age has done.")

As for hope, you say: "'Asa in dhakarta an tanjah" ("Perhaps, if you study, you will succeed"). But hope varies with the speaker and the one addressed. When I say to you, "Go to so-and-so; perhaps he will fulfill your need," or "Perhaps I will do something for you," the hope here concerns a human being. If the hope concerns God, it is stronger, as when you say: "'Asa Allah an yaghfira li" ("Perhaps God will forgive me").

So His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Would you, then, if you turned away, do corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ [Muhammad: 22] means: perhaps this may happen from you and is expected of you. Therefore, remain upon what you are upon of faith and obedience, and do not enter through the door of sins and disobedience.

﴿If you turn away…﴾ [Muhammad: 22] means: if you turn away from faith, or if you attain some positions, such as leadership, which bring calamity upon you.

﴿…do corruption in the land…﴾ [Muhammad: 22] means: among all of creation. ﴿…and sever your ties of kinship﴾ [Muhammad: 22] elevates the matter to relatives and kin: your corruption extends beyond people in general to your close relatives.

Or we may say: ﴿Would you, then…﴾ [Muhammad: 22] What turned you away from the truth that Muhammad brought, and why do you place obstacles in its path? The first of these is that you mock him, and that you describe him with what is not in him, by your saying: "Sorcerer," "Soothsayer," "Poet," and "Liar."

Then you harmed him in his person by abuse, in his body, in his family, and in his companions. Indeed, you plotted against him to kill him. What made you do that? Did you think and hope that by doing so you would wake up to the fulfillment of your desires for corruption in the land and the severing of kinship?

The Truthful, glorified is He, wants to teach us that messengers do not intervene, and heaven does not bring a new method, except when corruption has spread through the whole of society. This is because corruption has stages. The first is corruption of the self, and this has a deterrent from the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama), which is an immunity within the human soul that returns it to the right path and rectifies its conduct.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 24:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Will they not then ponder (afalā yatadabbarūn)?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]: this is an interrogative that conveys urging and encouragement to reflection. ﴿They ponder (yatadabbarūn)﴾ [Muhammad: 24]: they contemplate its meanings, look into its signs and miracles, and perceive them clearly. ﴿The Qur'an﴾ [Muhammad: 24]: it is the speech of Allah sent down upon the heart of His Messenger, which carries His method to the people, and it is a miracle that testifies to the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

To ponder it (tadabbur) means to reflect upon it, so that we do not stop at the surface and outward form of the verses, but dive into their depths, contemplate what they give, and seek out their secrets. In the Qur'an there are treasures from which we discover something new every day.

"It is clear in everything it contains, and from it I take as much as his mind can bear, every reciter."

As for His words, ﴿Or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]: meaning, they do not ponder the Qur'an; rather, there are locks upon their hearts, so they neither understand nor reflect. There are bolts upon their hearts that stand between them and engagement with the words of Allah. Allah is free of need from the faith of believers and free of need from the obedience of the obedient. He, glorified is He, is not benefited by obedience nor harmed by disobedience, and He possesses perfect and absolute attributes of perfection before He created this creation.

By His attributes of perfection He created, and by them He nurtured and provided, and by His self-subsistence He sustained His blessings upon His creation, including the disbeliever among them.

You remember the story of our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when a guest came knocking at his door seeking a need. Ibrahim went out to him and first asked him about his religion. He said: "I am a Magian," so he closed the door in his face.

When the man had left, Allah, exalted is He, rebuked His Prophet Ibrahim concerning this man, and said to him: "Because of spending one night, do you want him to change his religion, while I have sustained him throughout his life though he is a disbeliever in Me?" So Ibrahim went out after the man, caught up with him, and said: "Come, for my Lord has rebuked me concerning you." The man said: "What a Lord who rebukes His prophets concerning His enemies!" and he testified that there is no god but Allah.

Thus: Allah, the Exalted, encompassed all creation with the gift of lordship; as for the gift of divinity, He has reserved it for the believers in Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 47, verses 25–26:

The discussion here concerns the hypocrites (munafiqun). We have explained that hypocrisy did not appear in Makkah despite its hostility to the religion, but it appeared in Madinah, which embraced it, and from there it spread to the whole world. The reason is that one does not feign hypocrisy toward the weak; rather, one feigns it toward the strong. So when the Muslims grew strong in Madinah, hypocrisy was found among them.

Allah, exalted is He, says about them: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels...﴾ [Muhammad: 25]. That is, they were believers in their tongues, but their hearts were not believing ﴿after guidance had been clear to them...﴾ [Muhammad: 25], the truth, the right way, and the straight path that Muhammad brought had become manifest to them.

﴿Satan has enticed them...﴾ [Muhammad: 25]. "Sawwala lahum" means: he prepared for them, adorned for them, and made appealing in their eyes this course that deviates from the truth. Sawwala here means waswasa (whispered/insinuated), as He, exalted is He, says quoting him: ﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path"﴾ [al-A'raf: 16], and He says: ﴿He said: "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all"﴾ [Sad: 82].

Then he keeps to his limits, so He says: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [Sad: 83]. These have no authority for me over them, and I have no way into them.

It is remarkable that Iblis reveals his plans for misguidance, saying: ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾ [al-A'raf: 16], meaning on the path of obedience, in order to corrupt it for you. Therefore we have said: Satan comes to the mosque but does not come to the tavern.

And He said: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and behind them, and from their right and from their left...﴾ [al-A'raf: 17], from every direction, in whatever form, and through whatever door he finds a weakness in you. He comes to you through the door of wealth and love of possession, or through the door of women, or through the door of fame and love of being seen, and so on. For each person there is a key by which he enters.

It is among the mercies of Allah toward us that He taught us how to protect ourselves from him. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah...﴾ [al-A'raf: 200], because you cannot repel him by yourself, so seek help against him from the One who created him. When you seek refuge in Allah from him, he withdraws and shrinks. Therefore He named him "the whisperer who withdraws" (al-waswas al-khannas).

But if you try to repel him from yourself by your own power, the battle between you two will be long, because he is stronger than you and an expert in misguidance and leading astray; he varies the means for you and winds ropes around you from where you do not know, until he drops you into his traps.

It is among Satan's stupidity that he reveals to us his plans for misguidance. One who devises a plan to trap you does not disclose it. But he intended by this to establish the proof against everyone who obeyed him and listened to his words. Therefore he will say afterward: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me...﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

A person can know the source of a whisper: is it from his own self or from Satan? Satan wants you to be disobedient in every shade and by every method. If he fails with you through the door of wealth, he comes to you through the door of fame; if that fails, he comes through the door of women, and so on until he brings you down.

As for the self (nafs), it has a particular desire, and it holds you at that point and insists upon you.

Then you notice that Satan, as he said, comes at you from every direction except two: above and below. Why? They said: because these two represent the relationship between the servant and his Lord. In the lofty station of divinity, one directs his gaze upward, and in the humility of servitude, when he prostrates placing his forehead on the ground, acknowledging servitude to his Lord. Therefore Satan does not come at him from these two directions.

His saying: ﴿and He gave them respite﴾ [Muhammad: 25], He granted them respite and extended to them hopes so that they would persist in their misguidance and go on in their desires. ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down...﴾ [Muhammad: 26]. They are the Jews: the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿"We will obey you in some matters..."﴾ [Muhammad: 26], that is: we will support you and back you in some affairs that obstruct the progress of Muhammad's call.

In another verse, Allah, glorified is He, clarified what He left vague in the phrase "some matters," when He says: ﴿Have you not considered those who practiced hypocrisy saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture: "If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah testifies that they are liars. If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not support them; and if they support them, they will surely turn their backs, then they will not be aided﴾ [al-Hashr: 11–12].

﴿And Allah knows their secrets﴾ [Muhammad: 26], that is, what they conceal and what they hide of plotting against Islam. Since Allah knows that, He will surely nullify it.
