They are the Jews: the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿"We will obey you in some matters..."﴾ [Muhammad: 26], that is: we will support you and back you in some affairs that obstruct the progress of Muhammad's call.

In another verse, Allah, glorified is He, clarified what He left vague in the phrase "some matters," when He says: ﴿Have you not considered those who practiced hypocrisy saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture: "If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah testifies that they are liars. If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not support them; and if they support them, they will surely turn their backs, then they will not be aided﴾ [al-Hashr: 11–12].

﴿And Allah knows their secrets﴾ [Muhammad: 26], that is, what they conceal and what they hide of plotting against Islam. Since Allah knows that, He will surely nullify it.

I need to translate this passage from al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah Muhammad (47:27).

Here is the translation:

"That is: what is their state when they do that? And how will it be with them when the angels come to take their souls, striking their faces and their backs? How will it be with them at that time? Can they repel [it] from themselves? So then: why do they obstinately oppose? And why do they stand against the call and conspire against it? It would have been more fitting for them to support it."

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿That...﴾ [Muhammad: 28] refers to the evil end they will meet, including the angels striking their faces and their backs. Why? ﴿Because they followed what angered God...﴾ [Muhammad: 28]. They followed falsehood, which angered God against them, and more than that, ﴿and they disliked His pleasure...﴾ [Muhammad: 28]. They disliked the truth that leads to God's good pleasure. ﴿So He made their deeds fruitless﴾ [Muhammad: 28], meaning He nullified them and made them worthless.

So did they have deeds that deserved reward, which God then nullified? They said: Yes. They used to honor guests, relieve the distressed, and do similar good qualities. But they did good while God was not in their minds. They did it for fame, reputation, and people's talk. So let them take their wages from those for whom they did it, since they have no share in the reward of the Hereafter.

God says: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. And He says: ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows hard on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they earned...﴾ [Ibrahim: 18].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 47, verse 29:

That is: Do these people, in whose hearts there is a sickness [Muhammad: 29], think that hypocrisy [nifaq] will mean that Allah will never bring forth their rancour [Muhammad: 29]? That is, He will not make manifest their hatreds and expose what they conceal. Rather, He, glory be to Him, is capable of that, and He has indeed exposed them to His Messenger, made them clear to him, and laid bare their hidden hatreds. Therefore, in the verse after it, He says:

﴿And if We willed, We would surely show them to you, and you would recognise them by their marks...﴾

The deeds include both words and actions.

No intelligent person can fail to recognize the hypocrite from the marks on his face and his features. The liar has a mark that reveals him, and the truthful person's face has a radiance that shows his truthfulness, and so on.

As for His saying ﴿...in the tone of their speech..﴾ [Muhammad: 30], it means: in a slip of the tongue, or in twisting words and playing with them, as the Jews did when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ):  Therefore the pre-Islamic poet said:

"Whatever disposition a man may have, and though he thinks it hidden from people, it will be known."

God has exposed them in His saying: ﴿And among them are those who abuse the Prophet and say, "He is all ears." Say, "An ear of good for you: he believes in God, and has faith in the believers, and is a mercy for those of you who believe. And those who abuse the Messenger of God—for them is a painful punishment."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 61].

Their saying about the Messenger of God ﴿he is all ears..﴾ [al-Tawbah: 61] is like what we say: "So-and-so is wadiny," meaning: he listens a great deal. So God answered them: ﴿Say, "An ear of good for you..﴾ [al-Tawbah: 61]. Yes, he is an ear, but an ear of good, which hears what is good and guides you to it.

His saying ﴿by their marks..﴾ [Muhammad: 30] means: by their clear signs on their faces, ﴿in the tone of their speech..﴾ [Muhammad: 30], that is, their turning of words away from their commonly known meanings.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 47, verse 31:

The address here is to the believers who have believed in Allah and affirmed the Messenger of Allah. Allah says to them: ﴿And We will surely test you﴾ [Muhammad: 31], that is, We will try you and examine you with hardships and difficulties.

﴿Until We know those among you who strive and are steadfast, and We test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. That is, so that We may know who remains firm under trial among those who are in doubt and hesitation. Allah wishes to purify the believers and to test the strength of their faith, their patience and their endurance of hardships, for upon the shoulders of these people the call will stand, and it is a universal call which none can withstand except those whose faith is firmly rooted and whose creed is unshakeable, as the poet said:

"I care not, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for the sake of Allah."

These are the ones who were eager for death as others are eager for life. Allah granted them the station of martyrdom and freed them from death after they sacrificed their souls in His way, and He joined their life in this world to their life in the Hereafter.

His saying ﴿and the steadfast﴾ [Muhammad: 31] means: steadfast over hardships, the hardships of the call and the hardships of the obligations. When you reflect on the condition of this nation before Islam, you find that it was as though Allah, exalted is He, was preparing it to bear the message of Islam. It was a nation of war and fighting, mastering its arts and skilled in the charge and the retreat. It was a nomadic nation that did not settle in one place; their homes were on the backs of animals. It was an unlettered nation that had no system, no law and no way of life.

All of this qualified it to carry the call of truth to the whole world, to fight falsehood and to give people understanding of the religion of Allah. He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, so that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them...﴾ [al-Tawbah: 122].

Thus: Islam, in its struggle with its enemies, needs two forces for jihad: a force that strives to preserve the Word, and a force that strives to establish the truthfulness of the Word. Therefore testing and trial are a necessity. And the test ﴿And We will surely test you﴾ [Muhammad: 31] is not praised or blamed in itself; rather it is judged by its outcome. The one who enters the test and succeeds, we praise; the one who fails, we blame.

His saying ﴿Until We know﴾ [Muhammad: 31] — Allah says this while He already knows. So the meaning is: that We may know in the sense of actual realisation, so that the reality becomes a proof against its owner, lest he say: "If I had been tested, I would have succeeded."

The word ﴿and the steadfast﴾ [Muhammad: 31] indicates that there is hardship in the obligations and constriction upon the self; therefore some people bear them and endure, while others are straitened by them and despair.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 127]. So Allah is the One who helps you to be patient by showing you its good end.

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and they enjoin one another to truth and they enjoin one another to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 3]. "Tawassaw" means that each of you enjoins the other with it, for a person is sometimes patient and endures, and sometimes weakens and despairs; so sometimes you counsel me and sometimes I counsel you. The word "wasiyyah" (enjoining, counsel) in its very form is used only for a thing that is precious and valuable, which deserves attention and deserves that we be eager for it.

Thus these people did not limit themselves to disbelieving within themselves, but went beyond that: ﴿And they barred from the way of Allah..﴾ [Muhammad: 32], that is, they prevented people from believing in God, stood in the face of the call, and waged war against it.

Then ﴿and they opposed the Messenger..﴾ [Muhammad: 32], meaning they contradicted him and became hostile to him, to the point that they were in one side while he was on the other ﴿after guidance had become clear to them..﴾ [Muhammad: 32], i.e., the clear truth. The result: ﴿they will not harm Allah in the least..﴾ [Muhammad: 32].

All of these are failed attempts that will not avail them anything, and will not affect the course of the call. Why? Because the Truth, glory be to Him, would not send a Messenger to creation and then hand him over to them to kill him. This is one of God's laws in the universe: no messenger has been killed.

Yes, the Truth, glory be to Him, has told us about the Children of Israel that they used to kill the prophets, but He did not say "messengers": ﴿Say, "Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 91]. Consider here the phrase ﴿before (min qablu)﴾. No Jew, or even Muslim, may say that the Jews might kill the Messenger of Allah as they killed their prophets, because that killing was before Muhammad.

So: be reassured, they will not attain anything from the Messenger of Allah. This verse produced reassurance among the Muslims and despair among the disbelievers regarding this matter. They have indeed tried, but far-fetched is that for them.

Furthermore, their disbelief in themselves has a recompense, and their barring others from faith has another recompense, for they went astray and led astray. We understand from the phrase ﴿and they barred from the way of Allah..﴾ [Muhammad: 32] that the way of Allah is a moderate, straight path that draws people to it through moderate logic, sweet speech, and a beautiful, captivating method by which hearts soften despite their hardness.

It is natural for disbelievers to stand on this path, preventing people from faith and from hearing the Qur'an. Therefore the Qur'an recounts their saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it that you may overcome."﴾ [Fussilat: 26]. They were certain that hearing the Qur'an would affect them and incline their hearts toward it.

They did not stop at not listening; rather ﴿and make noise during it..﴾ [Fussilat: 26], they confused it so that it would not reach the ears of others. This is because they were people of language and eloquence, who savour words and styles and are moved by them.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and He will nullify their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 32], it means He will invalidate them and render them without benefit. The meaning of "their deeds" is either their deeds in barring from the way of Allah, or their good deeds which they performed in the world. Among their deeds was that they spent wealth in order to bar people from the truth through it.

On this God Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to bar from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be a regret for them; then they will be overcome..﴾ [Al-Anfal: 36].

They spent their wealth without benefit; people took it from them and laughed at them, just as happens with us, for example, in elections, where votes are bought with money: people take the money and do not give their votes, because they do not deserve them.

The second part of their deeds after wealth is fighting. Fighting has a reality in their conflict with the truth, and God calls out to them: O you who bear weapons to oppose the Messenger, take a lesson from the reality before you: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?..﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 41]. Do they not see that the land of Islam increases every day, while the land of disbelief shrinks and diminishes every day?

At Badr, He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours..﴾ [Al-Anfal: 7]: the caravan, which carried merchandise and wealth and whose guards were few, and the troop that came out to protect the caravan, led by Abu Sufyan.

The Muslims wanted the caravan that had the wealth, but God, the Exalted, had another matter in mind. They wanted the wealth, while God wanted to establish the truth, raise His word, and crush disbelief, and so that there would be no suspicion cast upon the Muslims that they went out only for wealth and spoils to compensate for their losses in Makkah.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿and you wished that the one without thorns would be yours..﴾ [Al-Anfal: 7], that is, the caravan. ﴿And Allah wills to establish the truth by His words and cut off the trace of the disbelievers, that He might establish truth and abolish falsehood, even if the criminals dislike it. When you asked help of your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ [Al-Anfal: 7-9].

Yes, the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, turned to his Lord and implored Him for help. And our master Abu Bakr said to the Messenger: "O Messenger of Allah, some of your pleading to your Lord is enough."

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was looking forward to victory over the troop of the troop of the nafir, the one with might, because he did not want wealth, but wanted to establish the truth and banish falsehood. Help from Allah is in proportion to patience: if you want to increase the help, increase your patience, increase your contentment, and increase your resolve.

Had God willed, He would have granted victory over them without fighting, but He willed that you fight them so that you might show your strength and superiority over them: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 14]. Had He defeated them by a cosmic sign from Him, they would have said: "It is a natural cosmic phenomenon; we have no power over it."

Likewise on the day of Hunayn: ﴿Allah had already given you victory on many occasions, and on the day of Hunayn, when your large number pleased you but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was constricted for you despite its vastness, then you turned back in retreat.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 25].

When the Muslims were deceived by their great number, He gave them a lesson to discipline them with, and their enemies prevailed over them. Then He reached them with His mercy and decreed victory for them at the end of the battle. In that same encounter He disciplined the believers and disciplined those who opposed the Messenger of Allah.

This teaches us a lesson: defeat for the believers is not because of their insignificance before Allah, but a training for them so that they correct their concepts and adjust their course. This lesson is clear in the battle of Uhud, as you know.

When they disobeyed the commander's orders, they were defeated; had they been victorious in this battle, the command of the Messenger would have become insignificant to them thereafter, and they would have said: "We disobeyed his orders at Uhud and we won."

Therefore they say about this battle: the Muslims were defeated, and Islam was victorious. Thus Allah nullified their deeds on both sides: the side of wealth, and the side of fighting.

The call here is addressed to those who believe, for faith is the basis of the command in ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [Muhammad: 33], and of the prohibition in ﴿do not render your deeds void﴾ [Muhammad: 33]. The believer is the one who hears the call and obeys the commands, because he knows that they come from a Lord who is Wise, the Creator, the Provider, and the Self-Subsisting.

Good lies in obeying Him, and loss lies in opposing His command. Therefore, when a believer is struck by a trial or hardship, he turns to himself and says: "What have I done? I must have departed from my Lord's method," so that he may correct what he has done.

Let us pause here at the repetition of the imperative verb ﴿obey﴾ [Muhammad: 33], once with Allah and once with the Messenger of Allah. There must be a reason for it. Yes, they have said: Allah legislates the general principle in summary form, while the Messenger legislates what clarifies and details that summary, as in the prayer, for example. Allah made it obligatory in summary, and the Messenger explained to us its times, the number of its units, and everything related to it.

So, obedience to Allah is in the general principle, and obedience to the Messenger is in the detail. When the verb is not repeated, as in ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger﴾ [Al 'Imran: 132], the command is one, upon which the words of Allah and the words of the Messenger of Allah converge.

The command also comes in another form: ﴿Obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾ [An-Nisa: 59]. He did not say, "and obey those in authority among you," but He made their obedience fall within the obedience to Allah and the obedience to His Messenger. There is no independent obedience to them, nor obedience to them separated from the obedience to Allah and His Messenger, for, as you know, there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator, and this is a legal principle.

As for His saying ﴿do not render your deeds void﴾ [Muhammad: 33], it means: because you perform good works and fine deeds, so preserve them and do not nullify them by committing evil deeds, in the sense of the poet's words:

"I have not seen among the faults of people a fault
like the incapacity of those capable of completing (things)."

And Imam al-Shafi'i says:

"If you are in a blessing, then guard it,
for sins remove blessings."

Among the shameful things is that a Muslim relapses and commits an evil deed after he has been granted success in a good one. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud: 114].

In the noble hadith: "From Allah's mercy toward us is that a good deed erases a bad deed, but a bad deed does not erase a good deed; rather, it requires seeking forgiveness." Among the most dangerous diseases that nullify righteous deeds is that they become mixed with *riya'* (showing off), reputation-seeking, hypocrisy, or a trace of *shirk* (associating partners with Allah), and we seek refuge in Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 47, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then they died while they were disbelievers..﴾ [Muhammad: 34]. It means: they died upon disbelief and did not make up for the matter by repentance before death overtook them. ﴿Then Allah will never forgive them﴾ [Muhammad: 34]. This means that if they had repented before the death-rattle (al-gharghara) and while the world still offered its room, they would have been forgiven.

In another verse He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills..﴾ [An-Nisa: 48]. Dying upon disbelief after guidance has become clear and evident to people is a sign of persistence; so how could it attain the mercy of Allah?!

Meaning of: ﴿So do not weaken...﴾ [Muhammad: 35] Do not become feeble in confronting the enemies, for you are facing them in battle. If they perceive in you the first signs of weakness, they will become bold against you and will covet you. Among the manifestations of weakness is that you call them to peace and truce ﴿while you are the superior ones...﴾ [Muhammad: 35], so act from this standpoint, and from this conviction, that you are the superior ones over them.

And why not? ﴿And Allah is with you...﴾ [Muhammad: 35], Who strengthens you and protects your backs. He, glory be to Him, is the mighty support who never forsakes whoever seeks refuge in Him, and He is the author of this method for which you are fighting. How, then, would He abandon you or hand you over to your enemies?!

Therefore: when the battle grows hot and the war intensifies, stand firm, and let neither their numbers, their multitude, their stratagems, nor their deceit terrify you, for Allah is with you.

Thus, in the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), when Pharaoh almost caught up with him and his people, so that the sea was in front of him and Pharaoh's soldiers behind him, one of Moses' companions said: ﴿Indeed, we are surely overtaken﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 61]. What did Moses say? ﴿He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 62] He said it with full confidence, certain of Allah's victory.

We understand from His saying, ﴿and invite to peace...﴾ [Muhammad: 35], a prohibition against our being the ones who seek peace and raise the white flag ourselves; rather, we should leave them to seek it. For this reason He, glory be to Him, says in another verse: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [too]...﴾ [al-Anfal: 61]. This is because they understand that seeking peace from your side is weakness and submission; and also, you should not seek peace because you are the superior, the mightier, and the stronger.

﴿And Allah is with you...﴾ [Muhammad: 35]. Whoever is in the company of Allah, Allah bestows upon him some of His attributes. Have you not seen, in the story of the cave, how they stood at the opening of the cave, and al-Siddiq said: "What do you think of two, whose third is Allah?" Since they were in His company, the Exalted, and since Allah cannot be perceived by sight, likewise whoever is in His company cannot be perceived by sight.

The meaning of ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 35]: "watr" (deprivation, loss) of a thing means losing it. The meaning is: He will not diminish anything from the rewards of your deeds; rather, He will pay them to you in full and more.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verses 36–37:

The Noble Qur'an gives us many images of the worldly life (al-hayah al-dunya), which in their totality show that it is a short, trivial life that deceives people and fools them. Among these images is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And strike for them the example of the worldly life: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, and then it becomes dry stalks which the winds scatter﴾ [al-Kahf: 45].

And here: ﴿The life of this world is only play and amusement...﴾ [Muhammad: 36]. This is a restrictive construction (uslub qasr) which affirms that the world is nothing but play and amusement, so the intelligent person should beware of it and not be deceived by it.

Play (la'ib) is to become occupied with something that does no harm but also brings no benefit. For this reason, some advanced societies began to refine children's play, so that it serves the purpose of entertaining the child and also teaches him something for the future.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: [...]

Play for the child occurs before legal responsibility (taklif), whereas amusement (lahw) is occupation with a matter that neither benefits nor profits, and that distracts you from a beneficial and profitable work, like the one who sits in a coffee house, for example, playing chess, and when the call to noon prayer is made, he does not rise to pray.

In Surah al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And when they see a trade or an amusement, they scatter toward it and leave you standing. Say: What is with Allah is better than amusement and than trade, and Allah is the best of providers﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11].

Whoever follows the verses of the Qur'an finds that it describes the world with this description in more than one place: play and amusement, in this existential order, because play belongs to children and amusement to adults, except in Surah al-'Ankabut, where He says: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play; and indeed, the Last Abode—that is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64]. Here the discourse concerns trials (fitan) that harm the Hereafter and keep you away from its reward, so amusement is mentioned before play.

Moreover, the very name of the world, ﴿The life of this world...﴾ [Muhammad: 36], suffices to belittle it and show its lowly status, for this description is the least of it. When you say "the world" (al-dunya), you recall its counterpart, "the Hereafter" (al-akhirah). If this is the lower (dunya), then that is the higher ( 'ulya); if this is perishable (fani), then that is enduring (baqi).

Nevertheless, the world is not disparaged in general; rather, it is disparaged only if what is blameworthy occurs in it, and praised if what is praiseworthy occurs in it. It is the field of the Hereafter (mazra'at al-akhirah), and one does not enter Paradise except through the deeds of this world. So the world is the subject matter of religion, whereas the Hereafter is the recompense, and recompense for a thing is not the thing itself.

We have said before that the world, in the eyes of the believer, is too important to be forgotten, because it conveys you to the Hereafter; yet it is too trivial to be an ultimate goal, because the goal of a thing is its end, and the world is not your end. Behind you is a goal more important than it, which is the Hereafter, the true goal beyond which there is nothing.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And if you believe and fear God...﴾ [Muhammad: 36], meaning: believe in Allah and implement His methodology in "do" and "do not." ﴿He will give you your wages and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ [Muhammad: 36], meaning: He will give you the rewards of your deeds in full without deficiency, and He will not take from you the wealth which He has bestowed upon you.

The evidence is that when He commands you to give charity, He considers this charity a loan which He returns to you with increase: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

As for His exalted saying: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments﴾ [Muhammad: 37]: the Truth, glory be to Him, does not ask us for our wealth, because man is created with love of wealth, and it is hard for him to have it taken from him. So Allah says: if He asked you for wealth, the asking would require insistence.

﴿He would press you...﴾ [Muhammad: 37]: He would insist upon you in asking while you dislike that, because it would reveal what you have of stinginess and what is in your souls of rancor and hatred.

When the resentments of souls appear, relations among members of society are corrupted, and you have seen this, for example, in the matter of nationalization (al-ta'mim) that took place; because wealth is usually earned with toil and sweat, so it is grievous to you that it be taken from you and given to others, and here resentment appears.

As for His saying: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you...﴾ [Muhammad: 37], it is like His saying: ﴿They do not ask people persistently [al-ilhaf]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 273].

They have said regarding ﴿and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ [Muhammad: 36] that it conveys the negation of comprehensiveness (salb al-'umum), not the comprehensiveness of negation (salb al-'umum). How? As when we say, for example: "Not all the students passed," meaning that some passed. Thus the negation here applies to the whole; this differs from saying: "All the students did not pass," which is the comprehensive negation, in which none of them passed.

Likewise, ﴿and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ [Muhammad: 36] means: all of it. So the meaning is that He asks you for a part of it, as happens in zakat, charities, ransom (fidyah), and expiations (kaffarat).

Play for the child occurs before legal responsibility (taklif), whereas amusement (lahw) is occupation with a matter that neither benefits nor profits, and that distracts you from a beneficial and profitable work, like the one who sits in a coffee house, for example, playing chess, and when the call to noon prayer is made, he does not rise to pray.

In Surah al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And when they see a trade or an amusement, they scatter toward it and leave you standing. Say: What is with Allah is better than amusement and than trade, and Allah is the best of providers﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11].

Whoever follows the verses of the Qur'an finds that it describes the world with this description in more than one place: play and amusement, in this existential order, because play belongs to children and amusement to adults, except in Surah al-'Ankabut, where He says: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play; and indeed, the Last Abode—that is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64]. Here the discourse concerns trials (fitan) that harm the Hereafter and keep you away from its reward, so amusement is mentioned before play.

Moreover, the very name of the world, ﴿The life of this world...﴾ [Muhammad: 36], suffices to belittle it and show its lowly status, for this description is the least of it. When you say "the world" (al-dunya), you recall its counterpart, "the Hereafter" (al-akhirah). If this is the lower (dunya), then that is the higher ( 'ulya); if this is perishable (fani), then that is enduring (baqi).

Nevertheless, the world is not disparaged in general; rather, it is disparaged only if what is blameworthy occurs in it, and praised if what is praiseworthy occurs in it. It is the field of the Hereafter (mazra'at al-akhirah), and one does not enter Paradise except through the deeds of this world. So the world is the subject matter of religion, whereas the Hereafter is the recompense, and recompense for a thing is not the thing itself.

We have said before that the world, in the eyes of the believer, is too important to be forgotten, because it conveys you to the Hereafter; yet it is too trivial to be an ultimate goal, because the goal of a thing is its end, and the world is not your end. Behind you is a goal more important than it, which is the Hereafter, the true goal beyond which there is nothing.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And if you believe and fear God...﴾ [Muhammad: 36], meaning: believe in Allah and implement His methodology in "do" and "do not." ﴿He will give you your wages and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ [Muhammad: 36], meaning: He will give you the rewards of your deeds in full without deficiency, and He will not take from you the wealth which He has bestowed upon you.

The evidence is that when He commands you to give charity, He considers this charity a loan which He returns to you with increase: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

As for His exalted saying: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments﴾ [Muhammad: 37]: the Truth, glory be to Him, does not ask us for our wealth, because man is created with love of wealth, and it is hard for him to have it taken from him. So Allah says: if He asked you for wealth, the asking would require insistence.

﴿He would press you...﴾ [Muhammad: 37]: He would insist upon you in asking while you dislike that, because it would reveal what you have of stinginess and what is in your souls of rancor and hatred.

When the resentments of souls appear, relations among members of society are corrupted, and you have seen this, for example, in the matter of nationalization (al-ta'mim) that took place; because wealth is usually earned with toil and sweat, so it is grievous to you that it be taken from you and given to others, and here resentment appears.

As for His saying: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you...﴾ [Muhammad: 37], it is like His saying: ﴿They do not ask people persistently [al-ilhaf]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 273].

They have said regarding ﴿and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ [Muhammad: 36] that it conveys the negation of comprehensiveness (salb al-'umum), not the comprehensiveness of negation (salb al-'umum). How? As when we say, for example: "Not all the students passed," meaning that some passed. Thus the negation here applies to the whole; this differs from saying: "All the students did not pass," which is the comprehensive negation, in which none of them passed.

Likewise, ﴿and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ [Muhammad: 36] means: all of it. So the meaning is that He asks you for a part of it, as happens in zakat, charities, ransom (fidyah), and expiations (kaffarat).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 47, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Here you are, you are those who are called...﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. (Ha) is a particle of alerting, to draw attention; (antum) is a pronoun of address; and (ha'ulaa') is a demonstrative pointing to this addressed "you." The addressee is thus the very same as the one pointed to. Therefore the verse combines three particles to emphasize the alerting and to add greater attention.

He used the alerting "ha" because the speaker is free to speak at the time he wishes; he holds the reins of the matter. The addressee, however, does not hold that, and does not know when he will speak so that he may listen. Therefore we bring an alerting particle so that he prepares himself and nothing of the speech escapes him.

So the Real, glorified and exalted, addresses them with all these particles to emphasize His call to them and His invitation to them to spend: ﴿You are called to spend in the way of God...﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. Who is it that calls? God calls them to spend.

Reflect here on how God honors and appreciates the efforts of human beings. Though He, glorified, is the Creator, the Provider, the Originator of causes, who granted you the strength with which you work, the mind with which you think, and the material you use, nevertheless He respected your role in directing the energy created by God toward something beneficial and useful, and He said to you: Spend as if the wealth were your own, while He is lending it to you as a goodly loan.

Likewise, you give your son his daily allowance, and he saves it, for example, in a piggy bank. Then circumstances arise in which you need what is in the child's piggy bank. So you say to him: Give me what is in the bank as a loan, and I will return it to you when I receive my pay.

He, exalted, says: ﴿Who is it that would lend God a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245]. So the Real, glorified, forbade usury in dealings among human beings, but made it lawful for Himself when He borrows from them. This is grace and generosity from God toward creation, in this world and in the next.

As for His saying: ﴿to spend in the way of God...﴾ [Muhammad: 38], it covers all the aspects of spending that God loves, from His creation to His creatures. He, glorified, is able to enrich everyone so that no one needs anyone, but He willed that hearts be joined, interests be intertwined, and creation be bound together by feelings of faith, such that the rich show compassion to the poor, the poor do not harbor resentment toward the rich, and the strong show mercy to the weak.

But when God called them to spend, there was among them a group that is stingy: ﴿Among you are those who are stingy...﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. These are the ones who do not understand the philosophy of trade with God, nor the outcome of spending. They do not know that spending in this manner increases wealth and does not diminish it. Recite: ﴿Who is it that would lend God a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him manifold, and God withholds and extends, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

Spending in the way of God is like a man who harvested wheat and put in the storehouse ten ardabs, for example. When he takes one ardab from it to plant the land anew, does he say that the wheat has decreased by one ardab? No, because he will take it back multiplied.

So: do not look only at what goes out, but also look at what will come, so that the picture is complete and the reckoning is correct. Even usury in people's dealings gives you an increase of five or ten percent.

As for your Lord, mighty and majestic, He gives you seventy, or seven hundred, or multiples of that. Recite: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a grain that produces seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains, and God multiplies for whom He wills, and God is all-encompassing, all-knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261].

For this reason the orientalists stopped at the saying of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: This contradicts the Qur'an, which establishes that the good deed is repaid tenfold. In reality there is no contradiction between them at all, because when I give a dirham as a loan, it gives me ten, the dirham I paid. So: he has given me nine, and when it is multiplied it becomes eighteen.

When the Real, glorified and exalted, urged us to lend, He taught us how to deal with the borrower, and said: ﴿And if someone is in hardship, then let there be a postponement until a time of ease; and that you give it as charity is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Baqarah: 280].

So the first stage is that you give him respite until he is able to repay. Then, after that, you may complete your kindness and be lenient with this loan, or part of it, as charity. This is the good for one whose soul aspires to lofty matters.

Then in His saying: ﴿Among you are those who are stingy...﴾ [Muhammad: 38] there is a fair assessment of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and a declaration of its nobility. Most of them spend and a few are stingy. Within the community there is one who spent all his wealth in the way of God, and one who spent half of his wealth in the way of God.

The giving and bounty in this community reached a level without parallel in history, where an Ansari would say to his Emigrant brother: Look at my wives; whichever pleases you, I will divorce her so that you may marry her. This is despite the known status of women, especially in the eyes of men. But this is generosity and sacrifice.

On the other side, you find this Emigrant Companion, our master 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf (may God be pleased with him), refusing this generous offer and praying for his brother, and saying to him: No, my brother, may God bless you in your wives, but show me the way to the market.

'Abd al-Rahman went to the market and traded, until he became the richest of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), to the point that they said: If he traded in dust, he would profit from it.

He had a thousand slaves. A man came and asked one of them: How is Ibn 'Awf among you? He said: By God, if he came to us while he was with us, you would not recognize him among us, because he dresses us in what he wears, and feeds us from what he eats.

Despite what is rooted in the human soul of love of wealth and love of possession, there are people who are disposed to generosity and munificence. They give without limit, giving as one who does not fear poverty. Look, for example, at the generosity of Hatim al-Ta'i when he says to his servant:

Kindle the fire, for the night is a night of cold,
and the wind, O boy, is a piercing wind.
Perhaps whoever passes will see your fire,
if a guest comes, you are free.

It is related that a group of people sat in the courtyard of Mecca speaking of the most generous people of their time, and they disagreed about that. One said: The most generous of them is Sa'id ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah. Another said: Rather 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far. Another said: 'Urwah al-Awsi in Medina is more generous than both of them. They nearly came to fighting. A wise man among them said: Send to each of these a man who will enter upon him as a passing traveler with a need, and see how he receives him.

They sent a man to 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, and found him riding out for hunting, with one foot in the stirrup and the other on the ground. He said to him: O son of the daughter of the Messenger of God, a passing traveler with a need. So he lowered his foot from the stirrup and said: Ride, and this saddlebag contains four thousand dinars, and in it is clothing of such and such, and in it is the sword of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, so take care of it.

Another went to Sa'id ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, knocked on the door, and the maid answered: Who is it? He said: A passing traveler, with a need. She said: The master of the house is sleeping, so what do you want? He said: A need. She said: Your need is easier than that I should wake him. By God, he has nothing but seven hundred dinars; take them and go to the camel pens, and choose for yourself a mount and a servant to serve it. When Sa'id awoke, she told him: Such and such happened. He said: Did you do that? She said: Yes. He said: Then you are free.

Then notice: to whom is the command to spend addressed here? To those who believe in particular, whom He addressed: ﴿O you who believe, obey God and obey the Messenger...﴾ [Muhammad: 33]. This is for the nobility of spending, its rank, and its doubled reward; He wants that the believer not deprive himself of this good.

Even the word (infaq, spending) is taken from (naafiqah, a market that is brisk). That is: brisk and profitable, because it is a trade with God. So do not think it is a stagnant, losing trade. Yes, it is a market that the Real, glorified and exalted, has established among His servants for a wisdom He willed, so He made some of them rich and some poor, some strong and some weak, and tested each of them by the other, to bring about this complementary movement within the community of faith.

For this reason we have said: God, exalted, wants the believer to work according to his capacity, not according to his need, because if he works according to his need and the need of those he supports, nothing will remain for the weak who cannot work. Moreover, the days turn in rotation; the strong may come to a state of weakness and need, or the rich may come to a state of poverty, and then he finds someone who gives to him, for man is the son of changing circumstances.

So: we can say that the spending that God has commanded us represents insurance for the believer's future, so that he does not fear for himself or for his children after him if circumstances drive him to need, and he may be confident that the believing community will extend a hand of help to him.

And the marvel in the matter of spending is that the Real, glorified, has exempted no one from it. Whoever cannot afford spending of wealth is bound by spending of speech. Recite the saying of God, exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find what to spend, if they are sincere to God and His Messenger. There is no path against the good-doers, and God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 91].

So whoever has means and is stingy toward one who lacks means, is obliged to advise him and awaken his heedlessness. If he does not do so, he is sinful. And if he has neither this nor that, God explained it in His saying: ﴿Nor upon those who came to you to be provided with mounts, and you said: I cannot find anything to mount you on...﴾ [al-Tawbah: 92]. What do they do? ﴿They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears, grieving that they could not find what to spend﴾ [al-Tawbah: 92].

This one who owns nothing but weeping and surging feelings that express his longing to spend and his desire for it, these feelings suffice him, and his deeds are reckoned by intentions. This situation may encourage him to strive to do something, to give anything at all.

The rich should beware of becoming a trial for the poor, when he withholds his right, so that the poor man complains and objects to God's decree that determined poverty for him and wealth for another. Do not combine upon him poverty and dissatisfaction with the decree.

Recite: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God, give them good tidings of a painful punishment. On the day they will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with them: This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard﴾ [al-Tawbah: 34-35].

The wise one is the one who lightens his load on the day when loads are heavy upon their owners, so that no one carries them for them. Whoever wishes to lighten his own burden, then at least let him give the excess beyond his need to one who deserves it.

The word ﴿Among you are those who are stingy...﴾ [Muhammad: 38]: stinginess (bukhl) is the withholding of the hand from spending. It is a motor process arising from firmly rooted impulses in the human soul, namely feelings of avarice (shuhh) which call its possessor not to spend.

For this reason He, exalted, said: ﴿And whoever is protected from the avarice of his soul, those are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr: 9]. That is: he overcomes this nature within him, and restrains the wildness of his soul until it obeys him and he spends.

Then the Real, glorified, makes clear the outcome of stinginess: ﴿And whoever is stingy, he is only stingy toward his own self...﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. That is: his stinginess arises from the avarice of his soul; or, he is stingy toward himself, depriving it of the reward of charity and spending, and depriving it of multiplied recompense.

So the word (ʿan, "toward/from") has given us two meanings: either it indicates the source of stinginess, which is the avarice of the soul, or it indicates the outcome of stinginess, which is the deprivation of the soul from reward, not the deprivation of anyone else.

The knowing scholars understood this meaning. Imam ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) was asked: I want to know whether I am of the people of this world or of the people of the Hereafter. The questioner said: The answer is with you. He said: How? He said: When a person enters upon you with a gift and another seeks a gift, to which of them do you show cheerfulness and with which of them are you pleased?

If you rejoice at the bearer of the gift, you are of the people of this world; and if you rejoice at the seeker of the gift, you are of the people of the Hereafter.

For this reason, some of the righteous, when a beggar came to them, would stand for him, welcome him, and say: Welcome to one who comes bearing my provision for the Hereafter without a wage.

As for His glorified saying: ﴿And God is the Rich, and you are the poor...﴾ [Muhammad: 38]: the Jews said: God is poor and we are rich, because He borrows from us. So God answers them: Rather, richness belongs to God. He is rich in His essence, independent of His creation, and He overflows from His richness, enriching creation by planting among them affection and mercy and making them love spending. So the rich does not swell with pride over his wealth, and the poor does not resent the rich because of his poverty. All are content and say: Praise be to God. It is as if all richness has its source in the Real, glorified and exalted.

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿And if you turn away...﴾ [Muhammad: 38], that is: if you turn away and refrain from the spending that God has commanded you, and do not believe what God has promised you of increase. Know that God will not abandon the weak, the poor, and the one unable to earn; rather He will replace you with someone better than you, who will respond to God's command and spend on God's creation.

﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you, then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]: not like you in stinginess, avarice, and withholding the hand from giving. Because you are My servant and My employee; if you oppose Me, I will bring someone other than you who is better than you. If you do not find goodness in one people, you will find it in others; and if you do not find it in one land, you will find it in another land.

It is well known that when Islam spread to the east and the west, people of generosity increased in the various lands of Islam, and they have stories and accounts of their generosity.
